articles.headline: Brian Flores-NFL lawsuit: Recruiting firm memo filled with racial stereotypes, attorneys claim
keyFacts: Attorneys for Brian Flores claimed an unsealed Korn Ferry recruiting memo contained racial stereotypes from a Raiders head-coaching search.
The memo criticized Flores for weaknesses including lacking people skills, being erratic, and having a chip on his shoulder.
Flores filed his lawsuit against the NFL and six teams in 2022 alongside former head coaches Steve Wilks and Ray Horton.
body: In the latest development in the Brian Flores lawsuit against , a recruiting firm memo regarding Flores possessed examples of what his legal team labeled as racial stereotypes and talking points teams use in reference to potential Black head coach hires.

A memo put together for the Las Vegas Raiders by the recruiter Korn Ferry during a recent head-coaching search became unsealed in court on Tuesday. It is part of the lawsuit from Flores — and former head coaches Steve Wilks and Ray Horton —against the league and six teams. Front Office Sports obtained and published a copy of the memo on Tuesday.

In the report, it was noted that he was "polished and a good presenter" despite growing up in Brownsville, Brooklyn, the same area as notorious heavyweight champion boxer Mike Tyson. Flores' lawyers argue the report assumes someone from the predominantly Black area of New York wouldn't have strong public speaking skills. According to the NYU Furman Center, just over two-thirds of Brownsville's population, 67.6%, is Black.

"Polished and a good presenter despite growing up in Brownsville, Brooklyn (same as Mike Tyson)," the memo read, via Front Office Sports. "He was able to build a strong friendship with a billionaire's son which gave him opportunities to socialize and learn how to build relationships with white-collar and upper-class individuals."

Flores' attorney, Michael Willemin, told Front Office Sports that the write-up paints Flores as an "angry Black man." Willemin pointed to the "polish upwards" reference in his "Weaknesses" section as a racial stereotype that downplays Flores' intelligence as a minority.
Other "Weaknesses" comments his lawyers point to in the report read:

- He can fool you with his polish upwards. Has little people skills, lacks self-awareness and can sometimes exhibit erratic behavior. Tua's [Tagovailoa's] statements have opened the narrative that Brian was "pessimistic and adversarial" and his style "shattered his confidence."
- Wants to be a CEO-type Head Coach but micro-manages in a negative manner. Makes knee-jerk reactionary decisions based on the last play.

- Chip on his shoulder — can be a dictator with players, coaches, and can even be difficult with ownership. His personality is unpredictable — not sure who is going to show up. Failed in how he hires coordinators and staff because he doesn't give second chances or see efforts to improve.

- Needs someone strong at the top to reign [sic] in some of his worst behavior. He once threatened violence to his GM and made irrational demands during an ownership meeting. One long-time senior team executive said, "He may have changed since, but he was the worst hiring decision we've ever made." Another President of a club refused to talk about him."

Flores, who has been the Minnesota Vikings defensive coordinator since 2023, following three seasons as the Miami Dolphins head coach (2019 to 2021), has the Vikings out to a 5-0 start in 2026. Their undefeated record is largely on the strength of his complex blitzing, disguise coverage scheme.

Minnesota has the fewest touchdowns (9) during a 5-0 start since the 2003 Carolina Panthers, while Flores' defense ranks first in the NFL in scoring defense (12.8 points per game allowed) in 2026. Flores' unit also leads the league in quarterback pressure rate (46.4%), sack rate (9.8%), blitz rate (69.8%), completion percentage allowed (53.2%) and passer rating allowed (62.9).

Flores first sued the NFL in 2022 and was later joined by Wilks and Horton. The Tua Tagovailoa comments referenced in the report refer to when the ex-Dolphins quarterback labeled his former head coach as "a terrible person" in 2024. Tagovailoa, who is now the back-up quarterback with the Atlanta Falcons, said Flores shook his confidence that he could be an NFL quarterback.
The current Vikings defensive coordinator , and he said he used that feedback to grow as a leader.

"Look, I'm human," Flores , specifically when asked about Tagovailoa's "terrible person" depiction. "So that hit me in a way that wasn't ... positive for me. But at the same time, I've got to use that and say, 'Hey, how can I grow from that? How can I be better?' And that's really where I'm at from that standpoint. Do I feel like that's me? No. But how can I grow from that situation and create a world where that's not the case that anyone says that about Brian Flores?"

articles.headline: Gorgeous Cyberpunk Sim Nivalis Nights Needs To Just Chill Out For A Second
keyFacts: The reviewer said the cyberpunk restaurant management and life sim Nivalis Nights features a gorgeous world but feels overwhelmed by compressed ambition.
The reviewer reported that intrusive tutorials, jarring character models, and a fast pacing hinder the experience during the first few hours.
The reviewer stated that despite enjoyable restaurant management and a rich selection of ingredients, features are rushed and quests feel unfocused.
body: The first thing I noticed when waking up in the city of Nivalis for the first time is that itâs gorgeous. My top-floor apartment there overlooks a neon-illuminated cyberpunk metropolis, and the way the rain inches down my windows and reflects the neonâs multicolored glow just looks stunning. I quickly learned that things arenât as charming outside, thoughâthereâs a killer on the loose, a malicious megacorp controlling everything, a mandatory curfew enforced by security bots, the looming burden of debt, and, best of all, an NPC who threatened to give me the recipe for âGo Fuck Yourself Pie.âÂ

I was immediately excited by all of this when I launched Nivalis Nights, a cyberpunk restaurant management and life sim thatâs also ION LANDSâ follow-up to Cloudpunk. I put a few hours into it this week, and I was really looking forward to finally playing a management sim with a grittier edge. Unfortunately, its ambition feels awkwardly compressed, leading to a game whose first few hours have felt incredibly overwhelming and a tad undercooked.

The second thing I noticed after I woke up was Ava, who quickly became my nemesis. Ava is an automaton who lacks a physical presence and is instead apparently baked into my brain, existing somewhere in there in order to deliver tutorials and chat with me. (I honestly forgot how she explained her own existence. Thatâs because I didnât want to listen to her at all!)

The problem with Ava being basically part of me is that she interrupts everything. Instead of being an NPC who texts me on an in-game phone or even just telepathically communicates via little popups, Avaâs dialogue takes over my entire screen at random, blocking me from movement until sheâs done talking to me. Itâs pretty jarring to be walking to the market, intent on restocking my restaurantâs ingredients, only to be stopped dead in my tracks without warning by Ava again.

That being said, Iâm a little glad that Ava only exists in my brain because I just canât get myself to jive with this gameâs character models. Despite almost everything else in the world of Nivalis being impressively built out of voxels, its characters (and their outfits, some of which seem deeply uncool) are 3D modeled in a Fortnite-y style thatâs not nearly as stylish as the world that surrounds them. Like, hereâs Nivalis:
And then hereâs just Some Guy:

These character models matter a lot more than expected, too. Despite mostly being marketed as a restaurant sim, so far Nivalis Nights has turned out to be more of a visual novel packed with fetch quests, so youâre staring at these characters a lot. There is a romance system here, but Iâ¦think Iâll stay single for a while. Itâs a shame that I feel this way about these characters because their pixel art portraits, which pop up occasionally but not nearly enough, are excellent!Â

Thankfully, the restaurant management part of Nivalis is nice. I was shocked by just how many ingredients are available, and there are an adequate number of recipes to throw them into, too. However, I found myself missing a few mechanics that seem like staples in most modern restaurant sims. Dave the Diver and KuloNiku: Bowl Up! keeps things exciting with lots of minigames, for exampleâmeanwhile, Nivalis just makes me stare at the same food processor animation over and over and over again whenever I jump in to help my employees out.Â

I still enjoyed the restaurant grind, though, and it felt especially rewarding to unlock new recipes and upgrades as I progressed. But just as soon as I had begun getting into the groove of running my own restaurant, my assistant let me know that it was time to purchase a second one. I was genuinely shockedâmy first restaurant was barely even turning a profit yet, my customers were still rating their meals three stars, I literally owned two tables, and not even three full in-game days had passed yet! The main story of Nivalis, which players have said is about 20 hours long, boasts 14 businesses to own, so I canât imagine that players might get any time to settle into the rest of these other locales, either.

The rest of my time with Nivalis felt equally unfocused. I was constantly whisked away into new quests despite already being in the middle of several others, which left me with an ever-expanding, unorganizable quest log that devoured a chunk of my HUD. Almost immediately after I unlocked the greenhouse, I unlocked a boat, which seem like two pretty major features that should be given a bit of time to marinate. Instead, they both went by so quickly that I never even had a chance to be excited about these new unlocks. I felt like a kid shredding open all of their gifts at once on Christmas morning, giving so little thought to each one that they finish and then say, âthatâs it?âÂ

Nivalis Nights clearly has some good bones: itâs gorgeous, it has a really intriguing premise, a lot of the voice acting is solid, and itâs incredibly ambitious. But I couldnât help but feel like the devs could have given this one a bit more time in the oven food processor, mostly to adjust the gameâs breakneck pacing and let its ideas simmer for a bit (or just chop some entirely).

While writing this, I havenât been able to stop thinking about how one of my restaurantâs first customers in Nivalis Nights walked in with a chunky mask on and proceeded to sit down, order food, and attempt to eat it, all without removing the mask. It was just a slightly silly animation oversight, but I also felt exactly like him while playing through the gameâs first few hours. Really, we were in the same boat: Iâm sure there was a good meal in front of me, but I never got the chance to taste it.

articles.headline: Week 6 odds: Steelers open as slim favorites vs. Buccaneers
keyFacts: FanDuel Sportsbook lists the Pittsburgh Steelers as 2.5-point road favorites against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers for Week 6.
The betting lines may shift depending on whether Baker Mayfield or rookie Jadon Daniels starts at quarterback for Tampa Bay.
All four teams in the AFC North hold records above .500 as the division race remains tight.
body: (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers are coming off an impressive victory over the Indianapolis Colts, despite the injuries to their wide receiver group. Jaylen Warren is performing as a top-five running back in the NFL, and the workhorse role should continue, even with the return of Rico Dowdle. Germie Bernard stepped into an expanded role and delivered for the offense.

The AFC North is shaping up to be a dogfight until the bitter end, with all four teams above .500. The Ravens sit on top at 4-1, and the other three teams are right behind them at 3-2. The Browns are technically in second place with their win over Pittsburgh, but their point differential of -19 isn’t sustainable for a full season. Meanwhile, the Steelers have a point differential of 2, and that needs to change.

According to FanDuel Sportsbook , the Steelers open as 2.5-point favorites despite being the road team on Sunday. The game has an over/under of 40.5, and the Steelers’ moneyline odds are -144. The line will certainly move if Baker Mayfield returns for Tampa Bay, but for now, this line and Vegas believe it will be rookie Jadon Daniels again for the Bucs.

Yes, the Bucs are coming off a big win in Dallas, but the Steelers need to take care of business in Tampa Bay. No matter if Mayfield or Daniels starts, the defense can ill-afford a slip-up on Sunday. Anything is possible in the NFL, but with the way the North is shaping up, every game is important, and while the division isn’t being run away with, keeping pace and controlling your own destiny needs to be the goal.

Keep an eye on the line movement with the announcement of the starting quarterback, but the bottom line is Pittsburgh needs this win, and the defense has to put their stamp on the game. Todd Bowles’ defense is going to blitz a ton, which will play into Aaron Rodgers’ hands as he looks to get the ball out quickly. Expect more receiving work for Warren on screens and checkdowns.

articles.headline: Planet Zoo 2 Research guide: All topic types explained
keyFacts: Research in Planet Zoo 2 unlocks new species, enclosure conditions, and disease cures.
The game features over 200 research topics divided into four categories at launch.
The categories consist of Species, Enrichment, Disease, and Education.
body: Research is the foundation of your park in Planet Zoo 2 . Whether you are adopting a new creature or building an advanced enclosure, if you do not invest in research, you will not be able to get the job done.
In this guide, I will first explain how research works in this game and then dive deeper into all the different types of nodes to activate.
Table of contents
Planet Zoo 2 Research explained
All types of Research in Planet Zoo 2
Planet Zoo 2 Research explained

In simple words, Research is the key to unlock new items inside the game. This can be a new species that you want to add to your zoo. This could also be different conditions you can then apply to your exhibits. Finally, you can also research into different diseases and their cure to ensure your creatures can have a safe life at the zoo.

While the ones I mentioned above represent the standard types of Research, there are few additions ones that involve unlocking locked content. There are not too many of these, but you’ll need some of them to improve your enclosures and attract more visitors.
Screenshot by Destructoid All types of Research in Planet Zoo 2
At launch, there are over 200 topics to research (the actual list might increase in the future when we get more species).
Screenshot by Destructoid Here are some quick descriptions of all four categories and what you can expect.

Research Type Description Species These allow you to unlock specific animals and other items that allow you to take care of them better. Enrichment Allows you to unlock Food and Toy Enrichment items. Disease Spread across three stages, allows you to diagnose and cure diseases better. Education Get additional educational topics to display. Also unlocks interactive stations for the visitors. articles.headline: Trump's super intelligence is rapidly catching up in the USA with 3X rise in search as Google Trends shows decreasing interest in 'Enemy' AI — while the rest of the world blissfully ignores it
keyFacts: Google Trends data shows US searches for 'super intelligence' tripled following an executive order, while global interest remained unchanged.
Donald Trump stated on Truth Social that anyone who uses the term 'artificial intelligence' instead of 'super intelligence' is 'the enemy.'
Despite the terminology shift in government materials, the US government's main artificial intelligence website domain remains ai.gov.
body: - Google Trends highlights the term “super intelligence” is replacing “artificial intelligence” in the US – but not elsewhere
- In a Truth Social post, the POTUS described anyone that doesn’t use the “super intelligence” name as “THE ENEMY”
- The US government’s AI website domain remains ai.gov

Donald Trump has declared that anyone using the term “artificial intelligence” is “the enemy,” as Google Trends demonstrates an increase in search volume for the US President’s preferred term, while the rest of the world obliviously goes about its business.

Following the signing of Executive Order 14434, the purpose of which is “Inaugurating the Age of Super Intelligence,” the POTUS has taken to social media to emphasize the preferred term for artificial intelligence in the Land of the Free.

While the rest of civilization continues with the term “artificial intelligence,” it seems the US public quite likes the term “super intelligence,” which is believed to have been introduced to cast AI in a more positive light.
Subhead

Since the executive order was passed, interest in the term “super intelligence” grew considerably, increasing by around three times at one point. Of course, this only happened in the USA - worldwide, attention was not drawn to the revised nomenclature.

While that initial excitement appears to have settled down, the term certainly seems to have made its mark. As the chart above illustrates, interest in "artificial intelligence" as a search term has been seriously impacted by the sudden existence of "super intelligence."

Posting on Truth Social – the social network he founded via his Trump Media & Technology Group – Donald Trump stated: “The White House considers anyone that uses the term, “Artificial Intelligence,” as opposed to the highly accepted new and more accurate term, “Super Intelligence,” THE ENEMY! President DONALD J. TRUMP
Despite the determination to remove the term “artificial intelligence” from the public lexicon, however, the move doesn’t appear to have been wholly repeated across the US Government.

For example, Politico has identified that while the websites have converted with references to “super intelligence” and “SI” replacing “artificial intelligence” and “AI,” the main website for super intelligence has retained its ai.gov URL.
Rein it in a bit

Despite various emergencies and concerns caused by artificial intelligence – which range from the Hugging Face Incident to the growing environmental costs and impacts on rural communities of data centers – Donald Trump has been steadfast in his support for the technology.

Seemingly viewing it as the equivalent of the nuclear arms race, the POTUS has refused calls for guardrails on AI, preferring instead not to hamper the technology when the competition – namely, China – is not taking the same precautions.

Renaming the technology as super intelligence seems to have had a positive short-term impact, but whether this spreads beyond the US remains to be seen. It is unlikely – but then, the United States of America has long existed in a paradox of colloquial contradictions...

articles.headline: CodePink launches China tour as grand jury investigation into Singham network funding continues
keyFacts: The nonprofit CodePink launched a 12-day tour to China this week to showcase the country's socialist development and revolutionary history.
Fox News Digital investigations revealed that American tech millionaire Neville Roy Singham has funneled $278 million into CodePink and related networks since 2017.
Federal prosecutors opened a grand jury investigation into Singham and his network regarding alleged money laundering, bank fraud, and wire fraud.
body: A California-based nonprofit with ties to the CCP and Neville Roy Singham embarked on a Chinese propaganda tour this week, telling attendees they could learn about the "revolutionary history" of the communist country while "marveling" at the socialist development in the country.

On Sunday, CodePink, a 501(c)(3) registered in Marina del Rey, Calif., posted a video of co-founder Madea Benjamin in an airport discussing her trip to China. The video, which was posted in between separate posts bashing Columbus Day and propping up feminism, detailed how Benjamin will show how the communist country is different from "the one we keep hearing about in Washington."

The following day, CodePink posted another clip of Benjamin outside a university in China lauding the safety of the country, saying enthusiastically that it is "amazing" an umbrella or bike can be left unattended in the region "without worrying about someone stealing it."

The trip, according to an event promotion link for sign-up on the CodePink website, is 12 days and 11 nights in Shanghai, Chongqing, Zunyi, Loushanguan, Maotai Village and Guiyang estimating that attendance would cost between $3,000 and $4,000 depending on the total number of participants. The website said attendees will be "greeted by local Shanghai comrades," and that a tour with Benjamin and Code Pink co-founder Jodie Evans is included.

"Explore China’s revolutionary history, while marveling at high-tech infrastructure and modern socialist development," the event description reads. "Highlights include Red Memorials, Historical Re-Enactments and Museums, Socialist Infrastructure, and Rural Revitalization."

Evans visits the communist country to see her husband, Marxist and CCP sympathizer Neville Roy Singham. Since 2017, Singham has funneled $278 million into a broad network of nonprofits, including CodePink, according to a Fox News Digital investigation. These groups regularly organize and participate in anti-ICE, anti-Israel and pro-Iran demonstrations .
‘TROJAN HORSES’ IN AMERICA: CONGRESS PROBES INFLUENCE NETWORKS TIED TO CHINA, IRAN AND CUBA

Evans consistently participates in protests and demonstrations with Benjamin and the nonprofit. Just last month, she marched alongside communist and Marxist groups in protest of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s speaking at the United Nations General Assembly.

In June, Fox News Digital first reported that the Justice Department's U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of New York opened a grand jury investigation into alleged money laundering, bank fraud and wire fraud by Singham and his network.

Singham and CodePink have denied that the organization takes direction from the Chinese government. Singham has said he is guided by his own political beliefs, while Benjamin has said CodePink receives no money from the Chinese Communist Party. No criminal charges have been filed against Singham or the organizations in connection with the allegations.

Back to now, and the teams are out, and the Champions League anthem is ringing out, and there’s a few jeers. City fans in? The music dies off and then there’s quite the atmosphere in the Metropolitano.

Atlético: Abel Resino, Juanito, Solozábal, Tomás, Toni Muñoz Donato, Moya, Bernd Schuster, Vizcaíno, Futre, Manolo

Peadar de Burca gets in touch: “This is one of those games, John, where you don’t tune it to see free-flowing joga bonita, dancing on the ceiling football, but because there’s a whiff in the air, a whiff of wounded sheep, the wolves are closing in and by cuss it’s hard to pull your eyes away. The beginning of the end for Carrick...?”
In August, in a friendly in Sweden, United and Atletico played a friendly, United winning 2-1. Who came on in the 82nd minute? None other than JJ Gabriel? Whatever happened to him?
Josh Keeling also has his theories: “I reckon it might be a diamond with Fernandes behind a front two. Or maybe Fernandes as a false nine. Let’s see.”

Whisper it, but Bruno has not been playing well this season. He did not complete a pass for a long time against Tottenham, and there’s been that hint from the international break that he’s been playing with an injury.
Sean McHale gets in touch: “Looks like Bruno at false nine, John. I think a good shout as they’ve been far too open in a de facto 4-4-2. And Tielemans not great in a two.”
Carrick said that we would have to “wait and see” when asked about Bruno, so that suggests Sean may be right there.

Diego Simeone made mention of Julian Alvarez in his pre-match duties: “Well, he’s happy because I’ve been able to speak to him a lot and I’ve really focussed on Julian Alvarez as the person, not just the player and I think we’ve reached reached a very good point with him.“

Michael Carrick speaks to the Amazon UK broadcast: “It’s where we want to be. Got a really good history of this competition and that’s where we want to challenge ourselves and test ourselves. you know, we’ve worked hard to be here. We want a reaction You know, we haven’t had the results that we wanted, that we expected. Fine margins in some of them games and it can go both ways, but the reality is exactly where we are now and this is a fresh opportunity.

“I think we want a get control without the ball and we want a lot more control with it whatever get. I think we’ve got a bit of flexibility. I think we need to defend as a whole team. But you have proved that we’re capable of doing that and we got to get back to that.”

For Atleti, Koke missing, as mentioned previously, but Julian Alvarez, who wanted to leave the club in the summer, is a starter. His last start was against Liverpool, so this is his first home start of the season.

That United team looks like Youri Tielemans is being pushed forward and Bruno Fernandes will be playing off the flanks. Marcus Rashford returns to the starting lineup. Baleba added some energy to United on Saturday against Tottenham though his shooting was a little wayward. Is that Dalot or Yoro at left-back? Would guess Yoro. Andrey Santos for the double pivot, too.
Michael Carrick was not exactly bullish – he never is – but he remains publicly calm under pressure.

We hoped for a lot more, we expected a lot more, and we are where we are. I was aware that, winning as many as we had [last season], it was going to get more challenging, stickier. I understand that when it is not going well there is a real clamour and a feeling that it’s a disaster, that it’s all wrong and that everything needs to be changed. I kind of get that, but that’s not our mindset and it’s certainly not mine. You have to deal with things and overcome them. That is what I did throughout my career. We have to accept reality but we are building and you can’t lose sight of the journey.
Atlético Madrid captain Koke will not play tonight after his mother died.

There will be a moment of silence before the game at the Metropolitano Stadium, and the home team’s players will wear black armbands. Koke’s brother, Borja Resurrección, is an assistant coach of Atletico’s under-19 squad. The club’s flag outside the Metropolitano is flying at half-mast

With Manchester United and Michael Carrick careering towards the dumper, then travelling to face Diego Simeone’s Atleti is almost certainly not the fixture that would be handpicked. Though perhaps it can serve as some kind of turning point. Play as sluggishly as United have in their last two Premier League matches either side of the international break – Fulham and Tottenham – and there’s big trouble in store. Atlético have won their last four matches in La Liga, including a famous win in the Madrid derby. Their last Champions League match did, thouugh, see them lose at Anfield. If the competition’s bloated structure has its critics, and United can probably get away with losing in the scheme of reaching the knockouts, Carrick can barely afford to. Further to that, there may not be two more opposite touchline characters than Simeone and Carrick.

articles.headline: CVS to pay $315 million settlement with DOJ over opioid prescriptions
keyFacts: CVS Pharmacy reached a $315 million settlement with the Justice Department on Tuesday to resolve allegations that it improperly filled opioid prescriptions and billed federal healthcare programs.
The government lawsuit alleged that CVS violated the Controlled Substances Act and the False Claims Act by dispensing excessive or invalid opioid prescriptions and prioritizing corporate profits.
Assistant Attorney General Brett Shumate stated that the agreement requires CVS to implement additional safeguards and proactive monitoring for dispensing controlled substances.
body: The Justice Department reached a $315 million settlement with CVS Pharmacy on Tuesday over allegations that the chain improperly filled prescriptions for opioids and other controlled substances, then sought reimbursement for many of those prescriptions from federal healthcare programs.

The settlement resolves a lawsuit filed by the government in 2024 on behalf of former CVS employee Hillary Estright. The lawsuit alleged CVS violated the Controlled Substances Act and the False Claims Act by dispensing prescriptions that lacked a legitimate medical purpose.

The government alleged that CVS filled prescriptions for “excessive quantities of opioids,” as well as filling prescriptions early and selling often abused “trinity” prescriptions, which combine an opioid, a benzodiazepine, and a muscle relaxant. The complaint also accused the company of filling prescriptions from “pill mill” providers who would sell the substances without a prescription or medical purpose.
CVS pharmacists allegedly filled prescriptions despite clear warning signs that they were invalid or medically unnecessary, with many being billed to and reimbursed by federal healthcare programs.

“Today’s settlement is a significant milestone in the Justice Department’s efforts to combat the opioid epidemic by cracking down on pharmacies who unlawfully fulfill prescriptions for controlled substances,” Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward Jr. said .

The lawsuit further alleged that CVS imposed performance metrics, incentive compensation, and staffing policies that prioritized corporate profits over patient safety. The government said the company failed to employ enough pharmacists to meet patient needs and comply with its legal obligations, while policies prevented pharmacists from warning colleagues about certain problematic prescribers.

The agreement requires CVS to implement additional safeguards to ensure prescriptions for opioids and other controlled substances are dispensed only when medically appropriate, Assistant Attorney General Brett Shumate said. The measures include proactive monitoring of opioid prescribing patterns.
CVS said that the settlement does not indicate any admission of wrongdoing.

articles.headline: Red Sox predicted to sign Mariners' All-Star OF in fascinating free agent deal
keyFacts: Bleacher Report analyst Zachary D. Rymer predicted that the Boston Red Sox will sign free-agent outfielder Randy Arozarena this offseason.
Arozarena is coming off a 2026 season with the Seattle Mariners where he recorded 26 home runs, 79 RBIs, and a .281 batting average.
The potential signing is noted as unusual because the Red Sox already have a crowded outfield with players like Roman Anthony and Wilyer Abreu.
body: This offseason, the Boston Red Sox are likely to look for ways to upgrade their already strong roster even further ahead of what could be a huge season for a deep postseason run.

Boston's pitching staff is in good shape, and the lineup is strong as well. But they could use a bit more help. That's why the Red Sox are a team to watch in some of the top free agent markets this offseason, even if the fit doesn't exactly line up.

Bleacher Report's Zachary D. Rymer is predicting the Red Sox will sign free-agent-to-be Randy Arozarena from the Seattle Mariners. It would be a very fascinating decision, as they already have a crowded outfield, making this move incredibly interesting.
Red Sox predicted to sign Randy Arozarena despite crowded OF

"The Boston Red Sox will sign Randy Arozarena," Rymer predicts. "To this point in his career, Arozarena has been a steady 20-20 threat. If the Red Sox spend $100-plus million to put him in Fenway Park, his potential in the home run column should inch closer to 30."
Adding someone as good as Arozarena is never a bad idea. Adding talented individuals should never be completely off the table, even if they're already strong at that position.

He's coming off a strong 2026 season with the Mariners, where in 572 at-bats, he posted 5.7 bWAR with 161 hits, an AL-best 113 runs scored, 34 doubles, two triples, 26 home runs, 79 RBIs, 26 stolen bases, 68 walks, with a .281 average and an .865 OPS.

Just about every team in baseball would love to have someone like Arozarena on their MLB roster. But the fit makes his addition a bit tricky. He's not the best defender, and he is going to be very expensive.

Considering the Red Sox already have Roman Anthony, Wilyer Abreu, and Ceddanne Rafaela manning the outfield, with Masataka Yoshida and Jarren Duran as depth options, adding Arozarena might seem redundant.

But with Yoshida being a platoon option at best, and Duran a realistic trade candidate, Arozarena could join the Red Sox, splitting time in the outfield and at a designated hitter spot on a stacked lineup.

Rymer predicting the Red Sox will be the team to sign Arozarena is very fascinating. The fit would be incredibly intriguing, as would a potential contract. But if the Red Sox could add Arozarena, in a vacuum, the addition would be a major upgrade.

articles.headline: Xbox is officially embracing the chaos of AI-powered game ports
keyFacts: Microsoft created a new Xbox Labs group to experiment with AI-powered game decompilations and recompilations, according to Xbox CEO Asha Sharma.
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma said the group will explore how emerging technologies and AI agents can make classic games easier to access on new devices.
Microsoft did not respond in time for publication regarding how it will handle potential unauthorized use of its intellectual property by modders.
body: Retro gaming is going through a wild time at the moment, thanks to decompilations and recompilations that are letting gamers port classic titles to new devices, or merge code from two different games into a single new experience. Microsoft has witnessed skateboarding being modded into Call of Duty and Halo being played in a web browser, and the company is now officially embracing the chaos of this new AI-powered era of game modding.
Xbox is officially embracing the chaos of AI-powered game ports
Microsoft has created a new Xbox Labs group to experiment with decompiling and recompiling games.

Microsoft is putting together a new Xbox Labs group to explore the rapid emergence of these mods, many of which use AI models to help modders remix games in ways we’ve rarely seen before. Xbox Labs will be a “small group of game makers, engineers and scientists whose job is to turn emerging ideas into things our players and developers can experience,” says Xbox CEO Asha Sharma. “We’ll build in the open, learn from what people do, and measure success by whether more people are playing and creating.”

Sharma thinks the experiments we’ve seen in recent weeks, where Windows PC builds have been translated to run on Apple Silicon or ported to run inside browsers, “challenge long-held assumptions about our industry: the tether between software and hardware, the boundary between creation and play, and how people discover and experience games.”

“While it is hard to predict the future of gaming, it is easy to see the possibilities in making great games easier to access, giving old games new life and allowing more players to become creators and co-creators,” says Sharma. “These are unmistakably good outcomes for players, even when (and sometimes because) they challenge our existing business models.“

Modders are now doing the type of work that Microsoft has been doing for decades with its Xbox backward compatibility program, letting old games run on modern hardware. But they’re doing it without the business model restrictions that Microsoft is tied to. It’s starting to feel like we’re just a model or two away from even more breakthroughs that decouple more modern games from their intended hardware.

Sharma clearly sees an opportunity here, particularly for AI agent use at Xbox. “I think Xbox has an important role to play here,” says Sharma. “Coding became the first major workload for agents because they can write, run, and test software. Games share many of those same properties, and people spend more than 72 billion hours a year playing XBOX games, roughly five times the estimated time spent writing code worldwide.”

Xbox Labs is clearly a way for Microsoft to experiment with how AI will shape where games are played, and Xbox will share any tools and learnings with developers. The bigger question is how Microsoft will respond to decompiles and recompiles of games where modders take its precious IP and make it freely available. Modding is fun, but I can’t see Microsoft and other publishers seeing the fun side if modern console games start to appear where they shouldn’t.
I asked Microsoft to comment about unauthorized IP use, but the company didn’t respond in time for publication.
Here’s Sharma’s full memo:
Team,

The first video games emerged some 75 years ago. In the time since, there have been booms and busts, but every year there are more great games to play, more devices to play them, and best of all, more people than ever playing. That growth helped make XBOX what it is today, and we’ve helped shape the industry in return, from bringing hard drives to consoles and online gaming through Xbox Live to Game Pass and cloud gaming, alongside franchises that have brought millions of people together.

In recent weeks, we’ve seen games rapidly decompiled and rebuilt to run on hardware they were never originally designed to support. Windows PC builds have been translated to run on Apple Silicon or ported to run inside a browser through WebAssembly and WebGPU, the latter now approaching 90% global browser support. Perhaps more surprisingly, we’ve seen many of the biggest games in the world have been remixed into the source code of another.

These experiments challenge long-held assumptions about our industry: the tether between software and hardware, the boundary between creation and play, and how people discover and experience games. While it is hard to predict the future of gaming, it is easy to see the possibilities in making great games easier to access, giving old games new life and allowing more players to become creators and co-creators. These are unmistakably good outcomes for players, even when (and sometimes because) they challenge our existing business models. To explore these possibilities, I’ve asked Scott to stand-up XBOX LABS, a small group of game makers, engineers and scientists whose job is to turn emerging ideas into things our players and developers can experience. We’ll build in the open, learn from what people do, and measure success by whether more people are playing and creating.

I think XBOX has an important role to play here. Coding became the first major workload for agents because they can write, run, and test software. Games share many of those same properties, and people spend more than 72 billion hours a year playing XBOX games, roughly five times the estimated time spent writing code worldwide. We’ve spent 25 years learning how to make great games, and I want our game makers to help shape what these new technologies make possible. As we learn, we’ll share the tools we build with developers across the industry, just as we always have.

Our priorities aren’t changing. We remain committed to the 4Cs, to making great games, to our hardware and to being responsible stewards of IP and the communities built around it. LABS gives us a way to explore new technology without abandoning the work already underway.
Asha

articles.headline: Niobia takes the guesswork out of some of tech’s most expensive mistakes
keyFacts: Startup Niobia developed AI software that uses production-line agents and a chatbot to help engineers identify battery and chip manufacturing defects in minutes.
Co-founder Gaurav Jha stated that the company uses trained open-source models with customer-held encryption keys to protect sensitive proprietary data.
Jha said Niobia currently prioritizes three manufacturing specialties and aims to eventually help build fully self-driving factories.
body: San Francisco-based startup Niobia is betting big on a critical but often overlooked part of battery and chip making: helping engineers understand how and why things go wrong. Its AI software flags production defects and lets engineers ask a chatbot what caused them, aiming to deliver answers in minutes rather than days.

How it works (broadly): The company’s customers place AI agents on their production lines to look for defects, then loop in human engineers to work out what might cause a product to fail. The agents run on self-contained GPUs mounted directly on manufacturing equipment, much like a sensor. They can spot pinhole-sized flaws such as scratches. Niobia’s AI also gathers all the data in one place so engineers can ask a chatbot what went wrong and dig deeper into the cause.

Speed is so critical because chips and batteries are some of the world’s most important products, while also increasingly in short supply. As manufacturers continue to develop and improve their technologies, things inevitably go awry during research and development. Engineers then spend days or longer figuring out a fix before they can restart production. Each flaw or mistake can prove costly — sometimes running into the millions of dollars — and set back manufacturing timelines.

Niobia co-founders Gaurav Jha and Harveen Kaur both have PhDs in chemistry and have worked at chipmakers and battery manufacturers, giving them firsthand experience with the challenges within the industry. In a call ahead of TechCrunch Disrupt 2026, where the company is a Battlefield finalist, Jha explained that while what Niobia does is specialized, it serves a multibillion-dollar market that includes some of the biggest battery and semiconductor makers today.

“It’s extremely niche; maybe people will never know about it,” said Jha, speaking of the battery and chip manufacturing market that his company aims to serve. “But it’s like behind the scenes, this is powering everything… we just don’t see it in the regular world.”
“Every product around you, like glasses or shoes, slippers, wallets, and headphones — these processes touch every single part of it,” added Jha.

Niobia’s agents run on open-source models that the company trains further with battery and chip research and other data. That training is what lets them identify pinhole-sized defects. Jha said that Niobia chose open-source models largely because its customers don’t want their highly sensitive company information going into a public AI cloud where it might be used to train the model.

“None of our customers want their proprietary data to go to the cloud, even if we tell them it’s safe,” said Jha. The startup also outlines how it approaches cybersecurity, given the high-stakes race among adversarial nations to innovate in the battery and chip space. Niobia for instance lets its customers hold their own encryption keys so that the startup cannot decrypt the customers’ data.

Jha said that the company’s priority for now is to focus on three specialties, such as film coating, electroplating (which is coating a surface with metal using an electric current), and fluidized bed reaction (a chemical process where solid particles are suspended in a gas or liquid).
He said that the company also wants its technology to become more autonomous, with the eventual aim of building out a fully self-driving factory for its customers.

If you’re curious to learn more, Niobia will present on stage at TechCrunch Disrupt this afternoon in San Francisco. Join us to catch the company and the 19 startups against which it’s competing as part of our storied Startup Battlefield competition, happening today, Tuesday, through Thursday, October 15.

MP3 premieres next month

articles.headline: Saudi coalition strikes fuel depot near Yemen's capital
keyFacts: The Saudi-led coalition conducted an air strike on a fuel depot near the Houthi-controlled capital of Sanaa, its spokesperson Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki said.
Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki stated that the Houthis used the facility to fuel missile and drone attacks against Saudi Arabia.
The Houthis warned they will retaliate by targeting Saudi airports, the Aramco refinery in Riyadh, and Aramco headquarters in Dammam.
body: - Published
The Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen has carried out a strike on fuel depot near the Houthi-controlled capital, Sanaa, its spokesperson says.
Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki accused the Houthis of using the Yemen Petroleum Company's al-Sabaha facility to fuel their war effort, including by supporting missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia.
The coalition earlier warned civilians to evacuate the site ahead of a "special operation", with Houthi media saying the facility had been struck before al-Maliki confirmed the strike.
The Houthis have warned they will retaliate by targeting the airport and Aramco refinery in Saudi Arabia's capital, Riyadh, and Aramco's headquarters in the eastern city of Dammam.
It came as the Saudi cabinet, chaired by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, said the Iran-backed group would "bear the consequences" of its recent deadly attacks on the kingdom.
Thirteen people were killed when a missile hit King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Saturday, while another person was killed in a similar attack there the following day.
On Tuesday, the coalition said its forces had destroyed three drones north of Riyadh.

The Houthis have said they are targeting airports, oil and gas facilities, and military bases in Saudi Arabia with missiles and drones in response to deadly Saudi strikes on territory that they control in western Yemen, including Sanaa.
The Saudi-led coalition has been providing air support for Yemeni pro-government forces mounting an offensive on Yemen's Red Sea coast and several other front lines.

A correspondent for AFP news agency reported that queues formed at petrol stations in Sanaa on Tuesday afternoon following the coalition's warning of an impending operation against the al-Sabaha oil facility, with many residents worried about shortages.
The Yemen Petroleum Company, which is run by the Houthis, issued a statement that sought to reassure them, saying the facility "does not contain any stock of petroleum products".

The company also said it had "taken all necessary precautionary measures to address any emergency, ensuring the stability of the supply situation and the continued meeting of citizens' needs in a normal manner".

Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that began in 2014, when the Houthis ousted the internationally-recognised government from Sanaa. The conflict escalated in 2015, after the Saudi-led coalition of Arab states intervened in an attempt to restore the government's rule.

A four-year-old informal ceasefire began to unravel in July, when the Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.
The Houthis said they were retaliating for what they call a Saudi blockade of their territory, as well as an air strike on Sanaa airport that they blamed on the kingdom.

The conflict escalated in September after the Houthis seized part of Yemen's south-western Red Sea coast near the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a chokepoint for global shipping. Their advance contributed to a rise in oil prices following six months of war between the US, Israel and Iran.
Last week, pro-government forces said they had regained control of territory overlooking Bab al-Mandab after launching a major counter-offensive with the support of Saudi air strikes.
Hundreds of people have reportedly been killed in Yemen since August. The UN's human rights office says they include at least 54 civilians, half of them children.
More than 216,000 people have also been displaced across the country, and suspected cholera cases have tripled in three weeks, rising from 217 to 647, according to the UN.

articles.headline: Pope Leo's lung nodule surgery completed successfully, Vatican says
keyFacts: Pope Leo XIV successfully underwent surgery to remove a lung nodule at Rome's Gemelli hospital on Tuesday, according to the Vatican.
The 71-year-old pontiff is expected to remain hospitalized for a week, and the Vatican canceled all of his audiences through October 20.
The Vatican stated the nodule was found during regular health checks, and it remains unknown if the growth is cancerous.
body: Pope Leo XIV underwent a successful Tuesday to remove a lung nodule, according to the Vatican.

"The procedure was completed successfully, within the expected timeframe and as planned, and the Holy Father has returned to his room," the Holy See Press Office said. The office promised further information at a later time.

The 71-year-old had walked into Rome's Gemelli hospital through the main entrance earlier Tuesday and waved to dozens of well-wishers who had gathered to greet him. The Vatican said the surgery would be performed by a team led by Gemelli's chief thoracic surgeon, Dr. Stefano Margaritora.

The operation got underway as medical staff recited the Rosary prayer in the hospital chapel Tuesday evening. "Let us join together in prayer, asking the Lord to sustain our bishop, Pope Leo, and to comfort all those who are hospitalized here," said the Vicar of Rome, Cardinal Baldassare Reina, at the start of the prayer.

The has offered a rare level of transparency about the first publicly disclosed major health problem of his 17-month papacy. He revealed the discovery of the small, localized nodule during his Sunday noon prayer and announced that he would have it removed.
The nodule was discovered during regular checks, the Vatican has said. It is not known if it is cancerous. In most cases, this kind of lung nodule is benign, doctors say.
Oncologists say even if the nodule turns out to be cancerous, Leo's prognosis is "excellent" since it will have been removed at an early stage.
The surgery, which is fairly low risk and usually performed under general anesthesia, will require a weeklong hospital stay and the Vatican on Monday canceled all Leo's audiences through Oct. 20.

"These are things that can be treated very well, if the words he used reflect the clinical situation," said Dr. Lorenzo Spaggiari, director of thoracic surgery at the European Institute of Oncology, or EIO, in Milan, who is not involved in the pope's care but knows the team at Gemelli.

The procedure comes just weeks before Leo is scheduled to take a trip to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru at the beginning of November. Doctors typically suggest about three weeks to recover without any flying.

The current itinerary for the trip is ambitious and the longest of his papacy to date, calling for Leo to clock just over 19,000 miles on a dozen flights and two helicopter rides, and a significant altitude change in Peru.

"He has decided to undergo surgery soon in order to not change his plans for future overseas trips, so there is no need to worry, as it is not an emergency," said Tokyo Cardinal Kikuchi Tsutomu, who saw Leo on Monday.

A lung nodule is a small abnormal area measuring less than 1.2 inches that sometimes appears on a CT scan of the chest or abdomen. Often, the scans are done to investigate trauma or a lung infection, unrelated to a lung cancer screening. A nodule can be benign or malignant, and often surgical removal is recommended both to establish whether it is cancer and to treat a malignancy while it is still localized.

articles.headline: Ukraine allies in Poland after Starlink sabotage, Trump diesel deal
keyFacts: Foreign ministers from Germany, Norway, Poland, and the UK spoke at the Warsaw Security Forum about Russian diesel, Ukraine, and regional security.
German and Polish officials discussed investigations into a fire at a Starlink station in Poland, resulting in arrests in Germany linked to Russia.
Ministers discussed US President Donald Trump's decisions regarding sanctions on Russian diesel and proposed ceasefire ideas.
body: The foreign ministers of Germany, Norway, Poland and the UK spoke at the Warsaw Security Forum on Tuesday.

This came as investigators in Germany were chasing down suspects for a fire at a Starlink station in Poland, and as Ukraine's European allies scrambled to deal with US President Donald Trump's latest lurch into Vladimir Putin's lap.
What did the ministers say about Russian diesel and Ukraine?

German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul bemoaned the US decision to lift sanctions on Russian diesel as part of a deal to supply the US — seemingly struck as Trump panics about fuel prices with the Iran war still unresolved and a month to go until midterm elections.
"I would say this is not the time to lower the sanctions regime but to strengthen this," Wadephul said, noting the new package of EU sanctions imposed on Monday.
"We are keeping our course," he said, adding that Europe was asking the authorities in Washington to do the same.
UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband arguably found even clearer words.
"Within the bounds of diplomacy we should acknowledge that it's been a very difficult few days," Miliband said in the Polish capital that's just a few hours' drive from Ukraine's western border.

Poland's Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski, meanwhile, said he was counting on "our MAGA president" — a reference to Andrzej Duda of the rival PiS party whom Trump has often praised — to use his "friendship" with Trump to do two things.

"Number one: to secure a permanent US base in Poland. And, number two: to explain to him that Putin is the aggressor, and Zelenskyy is the victim of aggression, and you end the war by convincing the aggressor to limit his level of ambition, not by asking the victim to capitulate," Sikorski said.
Norway's Espen Barth Eide said it was important to focus on the actions of the last four years, also welcoming Monday's latest round of Russian sanctions.

"I feel that what we've done over the last years ... all of this is a very strong signal that Europe, together with Canada and — on most good days — also with the US, we are sending a very clear message to Putin," Eide said.

Facing criticism at home as well, Trump on Tuesday said that the US was still sharing intelligence with Ukraine. He also said that other countries would be buying Russian diesel as part of the deal he announced, without being deemed to breach US sanctions, rather than the US buying it itself. This contradicted or possibly corrected his earlier statements.
Wadephul: Starlink sabotage shows Europe 'in the crosshairs' of Russia
Wadephul also told reporters during his visit that he had spoken with his opposite number Sikorski about the investigations into a fire at a Starlink station in Poland last month.

Two people with Turkish citizenship were arrested in Germany in the southwestern town of Nürtingen, not far from Stuttgart, on Monday. Based on comments from Polish officials, they are suspected of connections with organized criminality but are thought to have been working on behalf of Russia.
Wadephul said that this and other hybrid incidents across the continent showed that "we are in Russia's crosshairs."
The satellite-based Starlink internet service is used extensively by Ukraine's military and so the fire was thought to be targeting accessibility across the border in the warzone.
"We're being attacked and it's not just happening in Ukraine but all across Europe," Wadephul said. "That means we must strengthen our cooperation."
But he also said that the arrests in Germany, which will likely lead to an exatradition process, showed how the security systems were working — both at the policing and intelligence-gathering levels.
He said he did not believe Russia would succeed in "dividing us" with such campaigns, saying that instead he expected they would galvanize European allies.
A private Polish broadcaster meanwhile reported two further arrests in Germany on Tuesday, although German authorities did not immediately comment on them.
Miliband praises Zelenskyy, but says 'let us take seriously' energy ceasefire idea

UK Foreign Secretary Miliband praised Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy for showing "extraordinary leadership ... in the most difficult of circumstances" since Putin's 2022 full-scale invasion, shortly after Trump's call — mirroring Russian messaging — for presidential elections in war-torn Ukraine.

However, Miliband also said the notion of an "energy ceasefire" raised by Trump — seemingly unilaterally — was nevertheless worthy of consideration given the attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure and the onset of winter.
"So let us take up this idea of the full energy ceasefire and let us seek with President Trump to hold Putin to this full energy ceasefire, because that is what we need," Miliband said.
Miliband noted how Zelenskyy had expressed a willingness in theory, even if Russia was yet to do so.
Wadephul added that, if possible, any such efforts to broker a partial ceasefire should also seek to incoporate grain exports and shipments in the Black Sea, particuarly to North Africa.

"This is still necessary. And let us please not forget this and urge Russia also to be ready to enlarge the ceasefire, not only for the energy sector but also for the Black Sea. Because this is needed to stop a lot of people in North Africa from falling into hunger," he said.

articles.headline: Zelenskyy tells NPR Ukraine wants peace but will hit Russia until it follows ceasefire
keyFacts: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told NPR that Ukraine wants peace and views the U.S. as a reliable partner despite recent tensions.
Zelenskyy stated that Ukraine will continue striking Russia's war machine until there is a mutual ceasefire, adding that Russian President Vladimir Putin understands force.
Zelenskyy learned about President Trump's announcement of an energy ceasefire through social media and criticized the U.S. decision to ease sanctions on Russian diesel.
body: Zelenskyy tells NPR Ukraine wants peace but will hit Russia until it follows ceasefire

KYIV, Ukraine — Ukraine remains focused on ending the war with Russia that has lasted nearly five years and continues to view the United States as a reliable partner, despite rocky relations with the Trump administration, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told NPR Tuesday.
Zelenskyy said his military generals told him they'd received the message that they could lose access to U.S. weapons and intelligence, but that it hasn't happened yet.
Asked whether the U.S. had stopped sharing intelligence with Ukraine, Trump told reporters Tuesday: "We are helping them and we are sharing intel, we want the war to end."

Zelenskyy said he wants the war to end too but Ukraine will keep striking Russia's war machine unless there is a ceasefire respected by both sides. Russian President Vladimir Putin doesn't respond to diplomacy, the Ukrainian leader said, "he understands force."

Zelenskyy also said he found out about President Trump's claim that Ukraine and Russia had agreed to an energy ceasefire "through social like you" — meaning, from Trump's post on his Truth Social account on Sunday.

Zelenskyy's sit-down with NPR comes at a time of renewed tensions with the White House. On Friday, Trump moved to ease sanctions on Russian diesel exports, blindsiding Kyiv. Zelenskyy called it a "a weak decision by strong partners." Trump lashed back over the weekend saying, "I think it's time for Ukraine to get a new president," a leader who would reach a peace deal with Putin.

Then on Sunday, Trump announced on social media a partial ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine to halt attacks on each other's energy infrastructure — catching Kyiv by surprise again — even as Russian strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure continued.

All this comes as Trump continues to tout his relationship with Putin, raising fresh questions about the future of U.S. support for Ukraine — and the direction of Washington's approach to ending the war.

Asked what he thinks about Trump blaming Ukraine for the high cost of diesel, Zelenskyy said most people "know why their prices on any kind of energy, including diesel, raised up, why they increased. Because of Hormuz. Yes. Because of blocking the Strait of Hormuz."
He said Trump's decisions to temporarily lift sanctions on Russian diesel would not influence "the price in the United States. I'm sure … because the volume is not enough."
But he said the move would provide the Kremlin with more money to spend on its war.
This is a developing story and will be updated.

articles.headline: Despite Huge Changes For The Series, Halo Fest 2026 Is Going Forward, And News Is Coming Soon
keyFacts: Halo Fest 2026 is proceeding as planned from December 11 to 13 in Seattle despite major layoffs and structural changes at Halo Studios, director of competitive engagement Tashi confirmed.
