body: The big Halo Fest event planned for December is going ahead as planned, despite mass layoffs and other major changes at developer Halo Studios.

Halo Studios director of competitive engagement, Tashi, confirmed this and said there will be news about Halo Fest this week. Additionally, Halo Studios will release materials "celebrating the community and 25 years of Halo," while fans can also look forward to "relevant game info" about in-market Halo games.

"There's a huge amount of Halo fans who are looking forward to the event to attend or watch from home, and we're looking forward to providing a platform for the community to celebrate 25 years of Halo and each other," Tashi said of Halo Fest.

Halo Fest takes place December 11-13 in Seattle--the event is totally sold out. "No matter why you love Halo, whether it’s the story and characters, the music, the art and universe, or just playing with friends--Halo Fest will have something for you," Microsoft said of the event.

The voices of Master Chief and Cortana, Steve Downes and Jen Taylor, will appear at Halo Fest, while there will also be a range of community events celebrating the series. Some had expected Halo Studios to announce the next big Halo game at Halo Fest, but it's not unreasonable to think that plans may have changed.

Halo Fest is happening against a major shift for the Halo franchise following the gutting of Halo Studios and the transition of the series from Halo Studios to Activision. Halo Studios now employs a significantly smaller team that will support already-released Halo games like Halo: The Master Chief Collection and Halo Infinite, but future games in the series-- including the rumored reboot --will be made at Activision.

Halo Studios was rumored to be working on Halo 2 and Halo 3 remakes, as well as a new live-service Halo game. That was before the big changes, however, and it's been reported that Activision is working on a Halo reboot.

articles.headline: What is NVIDIA DLSS and how does it work?
keyFacts: Deep Learning Super Sampling is NVIDIA proprietary upscaling technology that renders games at a lower resolution and uses machine learning to increase performance.
NVIDIA offers different DLSS modes like Quality and Performance that balance image fidelity and frame rates by changing the initial internal rendering resolution.
NVIDIA has expanded the DLSS brand to include related technologies such as frame generation, ray reconstruction, and DLSS 5 for AI lighting effects.
body: What is NVIDIA DLSS and how does it work?
The company's upscaling software is truly powerful when used in the right situations.

If you own a recent NVIDIA GPU (or Nintendo Switch 2), there's a good chance you bought it partly from hearing good things about DLSS. Short for Deep Learning Super Sampling, DLSS is a proprietary upscaling technology designed to increase game performance. With DLSS enabled, your GPU will first render a game at a lower internal resolution, meaning it will need to draw fewer pixels. DLSS will then upsample the image to your monitor's native resolution using a machine learning algorithm trained by NVIDIA.

When it's implemented well in a game, DLSS allows you to effectively turn up the graphical settings higher than your GPU would normally allow at a native resolution while still getting a playable framerate. Alternatively, you run a game at lower settings and push the framerate even higher, which can be useful if own a high refresh rate monitor.
How does DLSS work?

The above gives a decent starting point for how DLSS works, but knowing a bit more can help with tweaking to get the most out of the tech and your GPU. As mentioned already, with DLSS enabled your GPU will first render a game at a lower resolution before upscaling the image it produces to whatever resolution you've set as the target. In almost every case, you'll want to configure the target resolution to match your monitor's native resolution. So if you own a 1440p monitor, set the output resolution to 1440p. In most games, you do this simply by setting the "display" resolution.

Now comes the more complicated part. DLSS can feel like magic, but ultimately it involves a compromise. The different machine learning models that underpin the tech are trained to interpret motion vectors, as well as depth and brightness information when they upscale an image. Over the years, NVIDIA's GPUs and models have gotten better at doing that, but at the end of the day, some amount of fidelity is lost any time you upscale an image. How much is lost depends on the DLSS mode you use, which determines the internal render (or starting) resolution your GPU has to upscale from:

Quality: When set to Quality mode, your GPU will render a game at 66.7 percent of your target output resolution. For a 4K monitor, that means you're starting with a 1440p image. With a 1440p monitor, your starting point is 960p. DLSS Quality offers the best image quality of the different presets, but expect only a moderate increase in frame rate.

Balanced: When set to Balanced mode, your GPU will render a game at 58 percent of your target output resolution. At 4K, that means a starting point of 1253p. At 1440p, meanwhile, you're upscaling from an 835p image. As the name suggests, Balanced mode is intended to offer a middle ground between image quality and a higher frame rate.

Performance: When set to Performance mode, your GPU will render a game at 50 percent of your target output resolution. That translate to 720p internal resolution when used in conjunction with a 1440p monitor and a 1080p internal resolution when the output is a 4K resolution.

Ultra Performance: When set to Ultra Performance, your GPU will render a game at 33.3 percent of your output resolution. This mode is intended to be used with 8K monitors. Expect a blurry image if used in conjunction with a 1440p or 4K monitor.

As a rule of thumb, if you're running a 1440p monitor, DLSS Quality is a good starting point for most games. If you're not happy with your performance or chasing an even higher frame rate, drop down to Balanced mode. Beyond that, the final image can get quite blurry. For 4K monitors, Balanced mode is a good starting, and then bump things down to Performance if you need or want more frames.
The many different features of DLSS
One of the confusing things about DLSS is that the branding has come to encompass a handful of related technologies that you can use in combination with one another.

Deep Learning Super Sampling: The initial version of DLSS arrived in 2019, following the release of NVIDIA's RTX 20 series GPUs. At launch, only a handful of games supported DLSS, namely Battlefield V and Metro Exodus, due to a limitation that meant NVIDIA had to train the algorithm specifically for the game it was meant to enhance. Since the release of DLSS 2 in 2020, that limitation no longer exists, and according to NVIDIA more than 1,000 games and apps offer DLSS support as of the start of 2025.

Following 2020, the biggest upgrade to DLSS came at the start of 2025 when NVIDIA reworked the algorithm to take advantage of a new transformer-based machine learning architecture and released DLSS 4. The new model offers better image quality, reduced ghosting and improved image stability. On older RTX GPUs, running DLSS 4 can result in worse performance relative to previous versions of DLSS due to a higher overhead. For that reason, NVIDIA gives users access to different DLSS "presets" (separate from the modes described above), which they can use to access older models.

Deep Learning Anti-Aliasing: Where DLSS is primarily designed to increase performance at the cost of image quality, Deep Learning Anti-Aliasing or DLAA does the opposite. Rather than upscaling an image, DLAA takes a native output and makes it more stable by reducing the amount of shimmer and flickering. Think of it a better version of temporal anti-aliasing or TAA. Not every game natively supports DLAA, but even in the ones that don't, you can use the NVIDIA app to add DLAA.

Frame Generation: Originally introduced as part of DLSS 3, frame generation allows NVIDIA RTX 40 series GPUs and up to generate a single interpolated frame from every two traditionally rendered frames, thereby increasing the overall framerate of a game. Frame generation is best used when your GPU can render a game at a consistent 60 FPS or more, and you have a high-refresh rate monitor that will benefit from the extra frames.

With DLSS 4, NVIDIA introduced multi frame generation, which allows RTX 50 series GPUs to generate and interpolate a greater number of frames based on a single traditionally rendered frame. As of the release DLSS 4.5 this past March, the current limit is six generated frames for every rendered frame.

Ray reconstruction: With DLSS 3.5 NVIDIA introduced ray reconstruction, a denoising algorithm designed to reduce artifacting from ray tracing effects. The algorithm works by sampling the light rays in a scene and then generating high quality pixels in between those rays. While ray reconstruction can offer performance gains, it's primarily designed to make games with ray and path tracing look better and more coherent.
What about DLSS 5?

DLSS 5 is an altogether different beast from the features described above. Rather than upscaling an image, DLSS 5 interprets a game's color and motion vectors to apply, in the words of NVIDIA, "photoreal lighting and materials that are anchored to source 3D content and consistent from frame to frame." In short, DLSS 5 is adding an AI filter to your games.

In early demos, the effect was uncanny, making it look like the tech was yassifing characters. But used more carefully, it can add more layers of realistic shows and textures to a game. Unfortunately, unlike other iterations of DLSS, DLSS 5 does not improve your framerate. It instead lowers it due to the overhead required to run the tech.

As of October 2026, DLSS 5 is officially available in just a single game: NBA 2K27. At this early stage, it's unclear if DLSS 5 will see widespread developer adoption, but that hasn't stopped modders from adding the tech to all sorts of games.

articles.headline: Echoes of Delicious in Dungeon ring out in Deep Dish Dungeon, a co-op dungeon crawler about making meals with whatever you can scrounge up that's out now
keyFacts: Deep Dish Dungeon is a new co-op dungeon crawler released on Steam that involves fighting skeletons, solving puzzles, and cooking meals.
Players must collect and unlock different recipes to gain stat boosts and survive the handcrafted dungeon.
The game supports solo play or cooperative multiplayer for up to three players.
body: I would really like it if someone made a Delicious in Dungeon game. It doesn't have to be official, it can be legally distinct! I've been asking for over two years now! I imagine I'll have to keep waiting, but luckily for me, a new game is out today which certainly feels reminiscent of the delightful (and morbid) anime, while still going for its own thing: Deep Dish Dungeon, a co-op dungeon crawler about making do with the ingredients you find that has a dash of Metroidvania elements.

On the surface, Deep Dish Dungeon looks like a… sigh, friendslop game (I don't like the term either). It certainly doesn't seem to be as curated as Big Walk, but the game's titular dungeon is apparently "handcrafted," so I don't imagine it's necessarily an infinitely replayable type deal. Amongst all the dungeoneering you'll be doing, which includes fighting skeletons and solving puzzles, you'll also be able to craft some tools and, importantly to your survival, cook up meals.

This is where that Delicious in Dungeon comparison comes in. I don't think it's quite as eclectic as the anime is, there are different recipes you can learn and unlock, but you won't exactly be having gourmet meals like Laios and co do. Sometimes all you get is a humble pie or corn and beans. It is important to make progress on collecting those recipes though, as the better recipes you get, the more options you have for stat boost. Turns out cooking your own meals is a worthwhile endeavour!

There are also a bunch of puzzly elements to figure out as you make your way throughout the dungeon, and enemy behaviours apparently require distinct reactions, you can't just go swinging your weapons willy nilly. I'm also not entirely sure where the Metroidvania elements come into it, but that's for you to discover I suppose. You can also only play with up to two of your friends (or enemies, I won't judge), but it can be played solo. I imagine it'll be a touch more designed around co-op play, however, so keep that in mind. If any of this takes your fancy, then you can pick up Deep Dish Dungeon on Steam right now.

articles.headline: House Dem pushes bill to abolish Homeland Security after Ilhan Omar raid, NYC ICE shooting
keyFacts: Rep. Delia Ramirez introduced the Reimagining Safety Act to abolish the Department of Homeland Security and Immigration and Customs Enforcement following recent enforcement actions.
The legislative proposal follows an ICE shooting in the Bronx and an HSI raid on the Washington home of Representative Ilhan Omar.
The bill faces long odds in Congress as both chambers are currently in recess ahead of the November midterm elections.
body: Rep. Delia Ramirez’s “Reimagining Safety Act” would also stop all immigration detentions in the US following last week’s shooting of Oscar Belgal by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents in the Bronx.

“Just this week, our communities were reminded that DHS is a weapon: pointed at a father shot in front of his 5-year-old and at Congresswoman Omar, who is using her voice to demand an end to fascism,” Ramirez (D-Ill.) told the Intercept in a statement.
“It is clear that now is the time to reimagine our safety, dismantle DHS, abolish ICE, and end the use of broad authorities to circumvent our rights and due process.”

DHS was established after the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks as part of a series of sweeping reforms aimed at making it easier to gather and share intelligence while streamlining Uncle Sam’s domestic security operations.

Throughout the 2026 midterm election cycle, Democrats in primaries across the country have called for abolishing ICE in response to the Trump administration’s aggressive immigration enforcement operations.

On Monday, agents from DHS’ Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) agency carried out a raid on Omar’s home in DC as part of a years-long criminal probe into the Somalia-born congresswoman’s immigration paperwork.

Federal agents presented evidence to a DC court to obtain a search warrant for the sitting congresswoman’s home, border czar Tom Homan told Fox News Monday, adding that a federal judge had signed off on the canvas.
Omar has claimed that she is the victim of a politicized weaponization of the justice system. Republicans have long raised questions about her immigration history and husband’s net worth.

The Reimagining Safety Act would replace DHS with a newly rebranded Department of Community Safety to fund violence intervention initiatives and other public safety measures, according to The Intercept.

Some DHS duties will be delegated to other departments and agencies, with the Justice Department taking over immigration enforcement, the Treasury Department handling customs enforcement, and the Department of Transportation managing the Coast Guard. It would also limit the ability of the Secretary of State to designate foreign terrorist groups.

“DHS is not rogue,” Ramirez added. “For 23 years, since its inception, DHS has been utilized by the government to target and persecute those they consider the public enemy — whether it is Muslim-Americans, Haitians escaping violence, Latinos yearning for a better life, or dissenting voices.”
Ramirez’s bill is a longshot to get through the House and Senate, both of which are on recess until after the Nov. 3 midterm elections.

articles.headline: Aston Villa star hints that £100m stadium renovation has had negative impact on form
keyFacts: Aston Villa defender Matty Cash suggested that the ongoing North Stand redevelopment at Villa Park has negatively impacted the team's home form.
The £100 million renovation has closed the North Stand for the entire season, reducing capacity and leaving fewer supporters in the stadium.
Manager Unai Emery also acknowledged the missing supporters as a handicap for the team while emphasizing the need to play better.
body: Matty Cash has suggested that redevelopment of the North Stand at Villa Park has affected Aston Villa’s form this season.
Cash and Villa have lost to Arsenal and Nottingham Forest in their three-match winless home run in the Premier League .
Villa still play their home matches at Villa Park, but the North Stand is shut for fans due to renovation work Getty
They led Brentford 2-1 in the 77th minute on Saturday but conceded moments later and settled for a 2-2 draw.
Fans inside Villa Park and those watching from afar have noticed that there is a stand full of supporters behind one of the goals.
Villa announced in April that the North Stand would be shut for the entire season due to ongoing works, including 12,000 new seats.
This will see the overall stadium capacity increase to over 50,000 as it prepares to host matches at Euro 2028 .
But Villa defender Cash believes its rebuild, which will cost a reported £100million, has affected their home form.
No excuses, but Villa Park is ‘different’
Speaking ahead of their Champions League clash against Fenerbahce at home on Wednesday night, live on talkSPORT, he was asked about how he has found playing with a missing stand.
“Our home form has not been what we want it to be,” he admitted. “Without sounding like we’re making excuses, because we have to deal with the circumstances.
“Obviously for the club and the platform, it’s really good to make the stand bigger, and the stadium bigger for capacity.
“But it’s obviously different, I’m not going to sit here and lie and say it’s not, it is different.
“But as I said, the circumstances, you have to deal with it as a player, you can’t make excuses, you have to play with what’s in front of you.
Cash has hinted that the lack of fans in the North Stand has impacted Villa’s home form during the season so far Getty
“When it’s done, it will be amazing but obviously at the minute, it is a bit different without making excuses.”
What does Emery think about the missing stand?
Villa boss Unai Emery also weighed on the North Stand’s absence at their stadium, and acknowledged as a ‘handicap’ for his side.
“Tomorrow we will be (at) Villa Park again with the energy we need. We have one handicap, it’s less supporters for this situation,” he said.
“But at the beginning of the season, the club decided it, and it’s something to improve for the future – not now, but for the future.
“It’s not excuses. We must try to be together, and without 7,000 supporters like (there) normally are in Villa Park, we must push everybody, and play football.
“One improvement in Villa Park is (to) play football, better football than we played.
Villa are aiming to complete the work on the North Stand in 2027 and ahead of Euro 2028, with Villa Park being a host venue Getty
“Compete better than we compete, to be focused more than we did, to be demanding more than we did.
“Those improvements are very important, more than the stand, and giving us lack of some supporters (who) normally were helping us.”

body: Former Sen. Sherrod Brown, a Democrat currently running to regain a U.S. Senate seat in Ohio after losing his 2024 re-election bid, has indicated that he would not support impeaching President Donald Trump.

If Democrats win the House majority during the midterms this year, they could seek to impeach the president along party lines next year — if that were to happen, the matter would then head to the Senate.

"I can't speak for everybody else, but I would not support an impeachment of Trump. There's just simply no reason for that, no matter what happens in the midterms," the former lawmaker told The Columbus Dispatch on Oct. 9
Brown's campaign and the White House did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment on Tuesday.

articles.headline: McIlroy: LIV Golf was half a good idea
keyFacts: Rory McIlroy stated that LIV Golf was half a good idea executed poorly and is no longer a threat after filing for bankruptcy.
McIlroy said he would welcome former LIV players back to the DP World Tour to benefit business, though some members disagree.
LIV Golf filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew its financial support.
body: Rory McIlroy says LIV Golf was 'half a good idea, executed poorly' but would welcome players back to DP World Tour

Speaking ahead of DP World India Championship, Rory McIlroy speaks about LIV Golf, saying breakaway was 'half a good idea, executed poorly'; Northern Irishman no longer feels LIV Golf is threat following PIF's withdrawal of support; McIlroy says he would welcome LIV players back
Tuesday 13 October 2026 18:59, UK
Rory McIlroy believes LIV Golf was "half a good idea, executed poorly" and the breakaway is no longer a threat to the traditional game as it tries to relaunch after filing for bankruptcy.
Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) ploughed in £3.7bn over four years, luring the likes of Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau away from the PGA Tour, before withdrawing its support this year.

That led to Chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings in the United States with a view to relaunching as LIV 2.0, having received a potential $300m (£227m) backing from BC Partners Capital providing a specified number of players re-sign for the new venture.

Rahm has already announced he will not be continuing and news this week that any player signing up for LIV will be barred from DP World Tour membership and Ryder Cup eligibility has delivered a crippling blow.

"LIV had probably like, half of a good idea that was executed pretty poorly," McIlroy told the Bloomberg New Economy forum in New Delhi, where he is playing this week in the DP World India Championship.

"They had a lot of capital but I think a lot of that capital was wasted in some ways and I think they could have used that money a lot more strategically and could have partnered with some of the governing bodies of the game and certainly could have done better things with it instead of just enriching tour pros who were already making a lot of money.

"BC Partners have come in and seen an opportunity (but) it looks like every day that goes by there's another player that was on LIV who is not going to join LIV 2.0 so I think it is going to be very difficult to get out of this Chapter 11 bankruptcy and go forward.
"But if they do it is certainly not going to be a threat to the traditional order of the game as it once was."
A more pertinent issue now seems to be what happens to those players quitting LIV.
The PGA Tour invokes a one-year suspension, denying them access until August next year, and while the DP World Tour has stiffened its rules its membership remains divided.

"I'm sure some members who stayed loyal would feel hard done by if these guys can just walk straight back in but, on the other side, having these players back on the tour is good for business and it can drive revenues up and everyone can benefit from that," added McIlroy.
"I would vote for them to come back. A rising tide lifts all boats and I think having some of these players back is beneficial for the business of the tours."
It is not a view shared by six-time DP World Tour winner Joost Luiten.
"Four years ago they didn't give a s*** about the DP World Tour," he told Today's Golfer.
"They made a decision to go after the money and now all of a sudden, the money is gone and they want to come back and act like nothing happened. I don't think that's right.
"If they think they are that good then show it at Q-School (qualifying school) and beat the guys. That's how every other guy that wants to play on this tour has to go."

articles.headline: Grand Theft Auto 6 rumored to be launching on PC sooner than anyone expected, but I wouldn't get my hopes up too high
keyFacts: A GamesBeat report claims Grand Theft Auto 6 will launch for PC in the first three months of 2027.
The report cites four anonymous industry sources familiar with the studio's plans, while Rockstar has not commented.
Rockstar's previous games typically had much longer gaps between console and PC releases.
body: A GamesBeat report claims that Grand Theft Auto 6—which still hasn't been announced for PC—will launch for PC sometime within the first three months of 2027. If correct, that means the game will drop, at most, just four months after its initial release on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S consoles.
GamesBeat cites "four industry sources familiar with the studio's plans" in its report, all of whom requested anonymity. Rockstar has not yet commented on the claim.
It's a surprising claim. Earlier this year, we predicted that GTA 6 won't likely appear on PC before November 2027, mainly because that's just how Rockstar rolls. We always have to wait.
The Unfortunate Timeline
- Grand Theft Auto 3: 7 months between console and PC release
- Vice City: 7 months
- San Andreas: 8 months
- Bully: 2 years
- GTA 4: 7 months
- Red Dead Redemption: 14 years, 5 months
- GTA 5: 1 year, 6 months
- RDR2: 1 year

Compared to that, a four month break between the console and PC releases, and possibly less, seems downright snappy, especially given how the gaps between GTA games themselves have grown over the decades.
Courtesy of Wikipedia:

Not only would a Q1 release of GTA 6 on PC be an unusually brief break, it also puts the game in the midst of the post-holiday hangover, when we're all doing our best to nurse our bruised and battered bank balances back to health.

And that, I think, would feel especially egregious in the immediate aftermath of this year's holiday season, which for gamers will be driven by the release of GTA 6 on consoles. Rockstar loves the double dip, but punching the button again so soon after the console release would surely be viewed dimly by a not-insignificant number of people who would prefer the flexibility and power of the PC, but really don't want to wait for it.
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Of course, if Rockstar or Take-Two confirms the GTA 6 PC release date really is that close—Take-Two's next quarterly financial report takes place on November 9, which might be a time for such a thing—some no doubt would wait for it, cannibalizing launch sales to some extent.

There's no shortage of people on social media saying they will indeed wait to buy GTA 6 if the PC version is indeed coming that quickly. That feeling may be even more widespread than it appears, given how much GTA 6 costs: At $100 for the premium edition and all the exclusive content it contains, you can understand why people might be more reticent about buying it multiple times than they were for earlier games in the series.
How about you?

Anything's possible, of course, and I would never presume to have a better understanding of these things than Strauss Zelnick and the rest of the GTA brain trust. But I also wouldn't bet on it—and for now I'm definitely taking all of this with a grain of salt. I've also reached out to Rockstar to ask about it, and will update if anyone answers.

Andy has been gaming on PCs from the very beginning, starting as a youngster with text adventures and primitive action games on a cassette-based TRS80. From there he graduated to the glory days of Sierra Online adventures and Microprose sims, ran a local BBS, learned how to build PCs, and developed a longstanding love of RPGs, immersive sims, and shooters. He began writing videogame news in 2007 for The Escapist and somehow managed to avoid getting fired until 2014, when he joined the storied ranks of PC Gamer. He covers all aspects of the industry, from new game announcements and patch notes to legal disputes, Twitch beefs, esports, and Henry Cavill. Lots of Henry Cavill.

articles.headline: Meta’s Audio-Only Glasses Are Nicely Made. They Don’t Solve the Deeper Problems
keyFacts: Meta launched new camera-free Ray-Ban smart glasses called the Clubmaster and Burbank, priced from $349 to $429 depending on lenses.
The new camera-free design offers lighter weight, smaller frames, and improved audio battery life lasting up to six hours of constant playback.
The glasses rely on Meta AI and must be paired with a phone app, offering features like music, phone calls, and an optional hearing enhancement mode.
body: I’ve started feeling self-conscious when I wear camera-equipped smart glasses out and about. It’s not hard to imagine why. Public opinion of smart glasses seems lower than it’s ever, driven by a combination of AI fatigue, privacy concerns and a general lack of awareness of what smart glasses can do or why anyone would want to wear them. Some places are also starting to ban them.

Meta’s addressed one concern, at least, with its new camera-free line of Ray-Ban smart glasses. Getting rid of the camera completely on the Meta Ray-Ban Audio means they’re smaller and lighter, and have better battery life, too. But they’re not as cheap as I’d have expected. The two models that are available starting this week, the Clubmaster and Burbank, run from $349 to $429 — just for the frames, depending on whether they have transitions lenses or not. Meta has more affordable self-branded smart glasses staring at $249, but those have cameras onboard.

I’m not sure why Meta didn’t make self-branded, camera-free glasses, too, which could have helped bring the cost down. I’m sure those are coming in the future, but in the meantime, skipping the camera seems to be more about design, privacy and extending audio battery life.
More from CNET
Are they a worthwhile addition to Meta’s lineup? Here’s what I think of them so far.
Wearing them: Lighter, for sure

I’ve been wearing a pair of the Clubmaster glasses, but without my prescription. That means perching them over my regular glasses or wearing them around the house without being able to see much. After all, the main thing that’s “new” here is the lack of a camera.

These glasses are definitely lighter and easier to wear, and the arms are a little smaller. They weigh between 43 and 47 grams, compared with a little over 50 grams for other Meta Ray-Bans. The front of the frames is a lot smaller on the Clubmaster model, but the half-metal design isn’t exactly my style.

Meta says battery life for constant audio playback is around six hours, a couple of hours more than the four I get from my Meta Ray-Ban Gen 2 and Scriber Optics glasses. For general wear, Meta gives the fuzzier estimate of “up to 12 hours,” versus eight hours for the others, which is harder to map out. Not using the glasses’ audio obviously makes the battery last longer.

The glasses work the same as other Meta smart glasses, with a touchpad on the right arm for tapping to start or stop playback and swiping to control the volume. I still activate it accidentally too often. A button on top activates Meta AI or can be set to launch music.
What you can do with them

Now, what would I use these for? I already find the audio quality on Meta’s latest glasses surprisingly good, and the microphones are excellent for phone calls. The audio seems a bit louder on the Clubmaster model, although the overall quality is similar. It’s still prone to being washed out in noisy areas because of the open design, which angles the speaker audio from the temples.
Obviously, I’m not taking any photos with these. That also means the glasses can’t perform any visually aware AI tricks or provide visual assistance.

Beyond music, phone calls and anything else you’d use headphones for, Meta AI is the necessary conduit for everything these glasses can do. They still need to be paired with the Meta AI phone app, too.

Meta’s FDA-cleared hearing enhancement mode, which lets the glasses function as a type of hearing aid for mild hearing loss, costs an extra $149 or comes with a Meta One subscription. I tried the technology as best I could at Meta’s developer conference last month, but I still don’t know how well it’ll compare with hearing assistance options such as Apple’s AirPods Pro. The audio glasses should, however, support hearing enhancement for longer on a single charge.
Why now?

Meta was clearly working on camera-free glasses before this year’s wave of backlash against its camera-enabled eyewear, though concerns about wearing camera-equipped glasses in public have been bubbling for a while.

But I also wonder what these particular models mean for Meta — and for its eyewear partner, EssilorLuxottica. The company has tons of eyewear stores worldwide and already makes a pair of assistance-focused audio glasses called Nuance.

The fact that these glasses are Ray-Ban branded rather than Meta branded lingers in my mind. I think they’re part of Essilor’s expanding range of more acceptable smart eyewear and likely aimed at customers who only want audio assistance.

But they feel a bit removed from the rest of Meta’s future-forward vision, which also includes display-equipped glasses and wearable neural bands. It could open up a path to display-enabled, camera-free glasses in Meta’s future lineup. It’s also likely an effort by Meta to find more acceptable ways to bring its AI to people’s faces, with or without cameras.
You’re still locked into Meta AI

Meta’s current Muse Spark-based AI on the glasses responds quickly and can provide live language translation and turn-by-turn navigation, set timers and serve as a general conversational research companion. But Meta’s support for connecting other services remains limited, and the privacy improvements promised for the company’s AI services in September haven’t arrived yet.

Fully agentic Muse AI is arriving on Meta’s glasses in the next year, but it’s unclear when. Muse already has an entire connected ecosystem of services, many of which require connecting other accounts to it. Some of Meta’s higher-powered AI models are now requiring extra subscription costs.

What this all means for Meta’s AI glasses over the next year is still a little unclear. They’ll increasingly become tools for tapping into those agents, perhaps to do work or monitor parts of your life. Currently, I don’t use Meta AI for much beyond short conversations about things I want to know on the fly.

Will Meta also explore always-recording “audio memories” in the future, capturing or summarizing conversations as companies like Apple and many others are already doing or promising? And if so, how will that be handled?

What I guess this means is that camera-free Meta glasses could gain acceptance in places where camera-enabled glasses are increasingly being banned. They could also offer a more reassuring option for people who want audio AI glasses but don’t want cameras. Still, most of the glasses Meta sells have cameras, and its AI is advancing so quickly that the shape of future smart glasses could change just as rapidly. They’re solid as wearable audio, but with Google’s glasses and a host of other audio glasses on their way in the next year, Ray-Bans are far from your only option.

articles.headline: The Paris Auto Show is full of interesting cars Americans can’t have
keyFacts: The Paris Auto Show featured numerous new car debuts and reimagined models, reversing a trend of declining automaker participation.
Stellantis showcased strong vehicle concepts from brands like Citroen, Peugeot, and Fiat at the event.
The author reported that the vehicles shown at the Paris Auto Show will likely not be made available in the United States.
body: Perhaps the days when auto shows debuted new models aren’t entirely over. The big trade shows for cars were a gateway drug for many, expos where you could see the newest models of today and the concepts of tomorrow. But automakers increasingly got tired of sharing the spotlight with each other. New reveals moved offsite to events the night or even the week before the show itself. One by one, brands pulled out of auto show after auto show until there was little left to see. And then the pandemic hit.

But the news out of Paris, where its auto show held media day yesterday, seems like we stepped back into a time when automakers would debut new cars aplenty. That retro vibe extends to the cars themselves, with plenty of familiar nameplates reimagined.

France’s Renault has a long and glorious history of delightful concept cars, and more on what it brought to Paris later. But the star of the show was arguably Stellantis, with strong work from Citroen, Peugeot, and Fiat, to name but three. But this article is meant to irritate you, because I’m pretty sure none of the stuff you’re seeing here will come to the United States. And it’s doubly irritating considering what Stellantis’ brands do offer us over here, doubling down on the same malign trends I saw back in 2020: did you know they’re about to relaunch a V8 Hellcat-powered Charger?
EVs can be small and cheap, apparently

The European concepts show us that, as those Kneecap chaps have it, there’s a better way to live. A sense of utopia was responsible for the original Citroen 2 CV; it had to be cheap enough for a farmer to buy it and rugged enough to get produce to market without breaking it. I’m not sure whether the 2 CV Concept also has to be able to transport eggs across a rutted field without breaking any (although the glove box is a clue), but Citroen says that affordability, lightness, practicality, and versatility were top of mind during the design process. The press release probably didn’t need to also say the company imbued it with distinctive character or charm; that’s quite obvious from the design.

articles.headline: Linus Torvalds is using AI to develop Linux kernel code now
keyFacts: Linus Torvalds released patches largely written with Anthropic's Claude Code to address a memory cache slowdown problem in the Linux kernel.
The experimental patches significantly increased read throughput in specific tests, but memory reclamation issues and performance regressions remain unresolved.
Torvalds stated that his use of AI marks an evolution from past skepticism to viewing it as a useful programming tool.
body: ZDNET’s key takeaways
- Torvalds just released a set of patches, which were largely written with Anthropic’s Claude Code.
- These new patches address an unsolved memory cache slowdown problem when using multiple cores and processors.
- Linus Torvalds had been moving closer to favoring AI, and this was the final step toward embracing it for Linux development.

It had to happen. Linus Torvalds announced to the world that he used AI to write code for the Linux kernel. Who’d thought it? Well, me for one. Over the last few years, I’ve seen Torvalds’ attitude change from skeptical to seeing AI as a useful tool for programmers and maintainers.

In his Git submission, he wrote, “The code, the test programs, the review behind the list above and the first draft of this text were done with an LLM coding assistant (Claude Code) under my direction.”
More from ZDNET
Tackling a shared-memory bottleneck

Specifically, the fix addresses contention in Linux’s page cache, which holds file data in memory. When several threads repeatedly read small amounts of data from the same cached file, they take and release references to the folio backing that data. Those reference-count updates require atomic writes to a shared cache line. This in turn forces processor cores to compete over it.

Doesn’t sound like that big a problem, does it? Wrong. In some workloads, it can really slow things down. Torvalds found that when eight threads issued 16-byte pread() calls against the same page on a four-core, eight-thread Intel Core i7-8565U laptop, the shared cache line accounted for 99.92% of the measured cross-core load, according to Hit in Modified cache line (HITMs). That slows work down considerably.
This isn’t just Linus scratching a personal itch. It’s been a known issue since 2024. Earlier attempts to fix it, though, have come to naught.

Torvalds and Claude Code’s proposed patches change when the kernel can reuse memory removed from the page cache. Rather than returning that memory to the allocator immediately, the patches defer reuse until a read-copy-update (RCU) grace period has elapsed. That lets a reader protected by an RCU read-side section copy data directly into a user buffer without taking a folio reference.

This approach trades immediate memory reclamation for a read path that avoids repeatedly updating a shared reference counter. The reported performance gains are substantial within that specific test. Eight-thread throughput rose from approximately 9.9–10.4 million reads per second to 30–33 million, while kernel cycles per read fell from roughly 2,950 to 725. Single-thread reads improved more modestly, from about 452–454 cycles to 408–409 cycles per read. Torvalds added in his pull request (PR) that “A machine with more CPUs, or more than one socket, should gain more; nothing bigger has been measured.”

This doesn’t mean Linux as a whole runs three times faster. Hardly! Instead, this describes experimental results from a particular small-read workload on Torvald’s personal laptop, which he had with him in Prague at Linux Plumbers.
Faster reads, unfinished memory management

That’s not to say Torvalds and Claude Code have fixed this issue. We’re far from being able to say that. The performance gains come with engineering trade-offs. Delaying memory reuse means pages can remain unavailable while the kernel waits for an RCU grace period. In his Git submission, Torvalds described that reclamation issue as “the part of this series that is least solved.”

There is also a regression when a read targets a user page that is not yet mapped. The new path incurs an additional failed exception before falling back to the existing implementation. As of Oct. 13th, the branch remained outside the mainline Linux 7.3-rc6. Whether it will ever be merged, and on what timetable, remains up in the air.
From AI skepticism to hands-on use
Torvalds’s decision to use Claude Code reflects a long-term evolution in his attitude toward AI. This hasn’t been a simple reversal from opposition to support.

In December 2023, he described AI as a potential aid to developers, saying, “I see AI as a tool that can help us be better at what we do.” At the time, his interest in AI was around how it could help identify bugs, rather than writing code. No one was giving serious thought to using AI to write serious programs (hard to believe now).

By late 2025, Torvalds was calling himself “a huge believer in AI as a tool, and saying he was more interested not just in finding bugs, but in maintaining code and reviewing patches. Generating new, serious code for Linux was still largely off the table. Still, in January 2026, he began toying with AI-assisted coding for a Python audio visualizer in a hobby project.
His latest remarks, reported Oct. 9 following a conversation with Dirk Hohndel at Open Source Summit Europe in Prague, were more enthusiastic.

“I used to think it was just not very good — but now I’m at the point where I actually really like using AI,” Torvalds said. “I think AI is a wonderful tool if you use it correctly and treat it as a tool, and I find it makes programming much more enjoyable.”
Even so, he cautioned, “I think that you need to be very careful using AI when you’re doing something real and important.” It doesn’t get much less real and important than Linux.

The page-cache experiment puts both sides of his position on display. Claude Code helped produce kernel code, tests, and review materials. The resulting branch shows promising benchmark gains, but also the unresolved memory-reclamation questions and performance regression that must be addressed before the experiment can become production kernel code.

Still, we’ve reached a turning point. Torvalds, arguably the world’s foremost developer and maintainer, is now using AI to develop new Linux kernel code. This would have been unthinkable even a year ago, and even now some people still struggle to imagine AI adding new code to Linux or any other important program.

articles.headline: Britain faces ‘new era’ of security threats from Iran and Russia, MI5 says
keyFacts: MI5 chief Ken McCallum said Tuesday that Britain faces a new era of security threats as Iran expands its attacks to target hard military sites.
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham stated that a recent incident involving seven men arrested near a U.S. air base was likely coordinated by Iran.
McCallum added that Russia remains the top aggressor engaging in hybrid warfare, while MI5 is also addressing risks from China, terrorism, and artificial intelligence.
body: LONDON — Iran is escalating its campaign of threats on British soil, expanding attacks beyond dissidents abroad and Jewish sites to now focusing on harder military targets, the country’s domestic intelligence chief said Tuesday.

MI5 Director General Ken McCallum was speaking less than two weeks after the United States rushed to withdraw its bombers from a key air base in England, with American officials saying there had been reports of a possible Iranian drone attack.

Giving a wide-ranging “annual threat update” at MI5’s Thames House headquarters in London, McCallum warned that Britain and Europe had “entered a new era of national security,” which he likened to the shift that came after the terrorist attacks of Sept. 11, 2001.

His speech comes at a moment of tumult not just for the Middle East and Ukraine, which continue to be ravaged by war, but also the rest of Europe, which has suffered so-called hybrid aggression from Moscow and Tehran including sabotage, arson and cyberattacks. European governments are now openly telling people to stockpile food and prepare for more of their taxes to be spent on defense, warning that Russia may launch a direct attack on their soil.
MI5 is now devoting more resources than it had during the Cold War to countering threats from countries such as Russia, Iran, China and others, McCallum said.
“Russia remains aggressor No. 1, as Putin’s Kremlin continues to lash out at the U.K. and its allies,” he added.

But another arch belligerent is Iran, whose leaders have been “attempting to expand their hybrid campaign” of “using criminal proxies to try to intimidate oppositionists, Iranian media organizations and Israeli sites,” the spy chief said.

“Much of this aggression has been aimed at British Jewish communities, with whom I want to express solidarity,” he said. But this year has seen a shift of “Iranian ambitions to come at harder targets, like military sites.”
Over the past year, intelligence operations have led to more than 50 Iran-linked arrests in Britain, he said.

McCallum made reference to the incident last month at RAF Fairford, the military base in rural England from where the U.S. had been launching bombers involved in the assault against Iran. He declined to give details, citing ongoing investigations and operations, but said the case was “not unique.”

Details are hazy, but in the early hours of Sept. 27, a member of the public called the police after spotting three vans in a country lane near the base. Seven men in their 20s, one of them a dual British-Iranian national, have been arrested and released on bail. Authorities said they found only gasoline in the vehicles.

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham told lawmakers in Parliament on Monday that the incident “is highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran, almost certainly directed” by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, the powerful political, military and economic group that holds huge sway in the country.
A week after the incident, Washington hastily withdrew its bombers from the base because, according to two U.S. officials, of reports of a possible drone attack against the site.

On Tuesday, McCallum downplayed fears that Iran could mount such a complex attack, saying it has so far been hiring unsophisticated criminals for operations in the United Kingdom. But he warned that could change.

On Russia, McCallum said its military and intelligence services “are once again escalating their attempts at hybrid warfare,” being careful not to trigger NATO’s Article 5 threshold, in which other countries would be expected to defend their allies.
“We see them scrambling to pay criminals to do their bidding,” he said. “The whole aim of hybrid tactics is to try to intimidate us.”

Within the U.K.’s “multifaceted relationship with China” — Beijing is a major trading partner to London — MI5 has been focused on efforts by the Chinese government “to conduct espionage, coercion or democratic interference.”
On Al Qaeda and the Islamic State terrorist group, or ISIS, MI5 still has to respond “to attempts to carry out mass casualty attacks,” he said.
But perhaps the gravest warning came when it came to artificial intelligence, which he said in the future could be used by terrorist groups and other actors to create new “bioweapons.”
And “beyond misuse of AI by human adversaries sit the potential risks posed by AI itself,” he said.

“Put at its simplest, human history has given us no experience of facing an actor which is smarter than we are. Is capable of out-thinking us. This is genuinely novel. And deserves the serious attention it is getting, including in MI5.”

articles.headline: Over 1 Million Characters Have Been Made in the WoW Forever Beta
keyFacts: Community data shows that over one million characters have been created in the World of Warcraft Forever beta.
Humans are the most popular Alliance race and Undead are the most popular Horde race in the beta.
The full game is scheduled to launch on November 4, and current beta characters will be wiped.
body: It's no secret that World of Warcraft Forever has been incredibly popular since entering its beta last month, but now, over 1 million characters have been made.

According to classicplus.io, a community website that snapshots data from WoW Forever, 1,003,125 characters have been made in the Classic Plus mode so far. That's a lot, considering that to even make a character you need to have access to the beta, which is primarily done by buying the $30 Skyborne pack.

But even though most people will have to buy access to the Skyborne race to play in the beta, the Skyborne aren't the most popular race on either faction. For both Alliance and Horde players, the fancy blue elves only represent 18.7% of characters created. Instead, for Alliance players, Humans are much more popular at 32.3%, whereas Horde players seem to prefer Undead characters, at 33.5% of the population.

It's important to remember that while 1 million characters might not seem like a lot in a game that had a peak of 12 million players 16 years ago, WoW Forever hasn't even launched yet. The full game doesn't come out until November 4, and anyone playing the beta now only has access to limited parts of the world. At the time of writing, the level cap in the beta is level 30, and characters will be wiped when the full game launches next month.

So, it's impressive that so many people are playing the game right now, knowing that everything they earn in the game is going to vanish in less than a month. It's a good sign for Blizzard, and suggests that when Forever launches, it's going to be incredibly popular, even if it has to go head-to-head with Grand Theft Auto 6, which launches two weeks later — though I imagine there isn't much crossover between the two games.

Even when WoW Forever first entered its beta last month, Blizzard developers were shocked at how popular it was. One developer even said the beta was putting up "the craziest numbers" they'd ever seen. However, Forever hasn't been free of its own controversies. Blizzard has cracked down on players' names, leading some to think they've been unfairly targeted . And, Blizzard is also cracking down on gold selling, leading to WoW streamers getting caught in the crossfire . But, Blizzard has also added the beloved "Kyle's Gone Missing" quest, even though it wasn't added until Burning Crusade, and everybody seems to love that.

articles.headline: Liverpool's Wirtz problem - does he need to be dropped?
keyFacts: Liverpool midfielder Florian Wirtz has struggled to consistently impact games and create chances following his 116 million pound transfer.
Pundits Steven Warnock and Jamie Carragher said that Wirtz's poor performances mean he should be dropped from the team.
Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola defended Wirtz, stating the player has had good games and the team's issues are collective.
body: - Published
At the end of the 2024-25 season, Liverpool head coach Arne Slot flew to the south of France to honour talks with Rayan Cherki.
Cherki was on Liverpool's shortlist in their hunt for an attacking midfielder but the main target was Florian Wirtz - who was also wanted by Bayern Munich and Manchester City.
Once Wirtz said his preference was to move to Anfield and join the then-Premier League champions, the Â£116m deal became a formality.
At the time, his arrival felt like a quality acquisition for Liverpool, but more than a year on things are still not clicking.
The German has scored seven goals and provided 11 assists over 56 Reds appearances, but had no goal involvements against any of the top-10 teams in the Premier League last season.
This term, Wirtz has started every game in the league and Champions League so far - managing just one assist across seven matches.

Those struggles were summed up on Sunday against Manchester City when new Reds boss Andoni Iraola - who succeeded Slot in the summer - replaced Wirtz with Trey Nyoni in the 66th minute, shortly after Ryan Gravenberch was sent off and Erling Haaland broke the deadlock.

Wirtz is only 23 but so is Cherki, who put the icing on the cake in City's 3-0 win at Anfield with an exquisite goal - the kind we have become used to seeing since his Â£30m move from Lyon in June 2025.
Cherki cost less than a third of what Liverpool paid for Wirtz, but has already scored 16 goals and provided 18 assists in 65 City appearances.
The France attacker has also shown an ability to provide crucial game-changing moments. Liverpool fans haven't seen anywhere near enough of that from Wirtz yet.
"Wirtz has so much ability. I wish I had that ability because he just glides. He makes it look effortless - but he doesn't hurt teams," former Liverpool defender Steven Warnock told BBC Radio 5 Live.
"He doesn't impact the game enough. He drifts in and out of games. He's here for 10 or 20 seconds and then he disappears for five or 10 minutes and you think where is he now?"
After Liverpool's defeat by Man City, Jamie Carragher said it was time for Iraola to drop Wirtz.
"I think he needs to come out of the team, I said that last time out and I'm going to say it again," Carragher told Sky Sports.

"Liverpool played well [against Man City] for a lot of the game before the Gravenberch red card but they didn't create a chance, so they have a real problem with scoring goals and creating chances and that's what you got Wirtz for.

"He's not giving you anything defensively and he's not giving you anything going the other way. I don't want anyone to pile in on the lad but I think we're justified in saying we need more and we can't wait."
'Anyone who loves football can see Wirtz is outstanding'

Given that Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai are all currently sidelined, it would be a big call to drop Wirtz - but Liverpool have two games every week between now and the November international break.

With Gravenberch suspended for Saturday's trip to Brentford, Iraola will likely keep the Dutch midfielder in for Wednesday's Champions League game against LASK in Austria and give a start to Nyoni. More changes are expected from Sunday's defeat.

When it comes to the intensity of the top flight, Wirtz is still finding his feet, but his best performance this season came in the Champions League against Atletico Madrid and he was unlucky not to get an assist when Bradley Barcola fired wide.
Asked on Tuesday if Wirtz needed more time, Iraola defended his player and said: "The other day, he probably he didn't have his best game but he has had good games with us this season.
"Everyone starts looking for answers. He had some good performances in the national team - he scored one goal and he will have better or worse games.
"But I would like to look at it more collectively and more how they help us play and get results and after that I don't care who scores. I think it's a more collective thing."
Seeing Wirtz excel for Germany under Jurgen Klopp is proof - if it was needed - as to why he was seen as one of the hottest talents in world football when he joined Liverpool.
"Attacking players always need a functioning team that works well around them. Anyone who loves football can still see how outstanding Florian is as a player," Klopp said recently.
That is also a view shared by Steven Gerrard.

"I can just picture him beating himself up on how his Liverpool thing has started. This kid is a major talent in my opinion. I've seen enough to believe and give him a chance. I think he needs help and support now," Gerrard told The Overlap.

Wirtz created 95 chances from open play in all competitions last season - at least 27 more than any other Liverpool player - and his fizzing pass for Victor Munoz's equaliser against Nottingham Forest in August showed a glimpse of his class, but those moments have been few and far in between.

Against City at the weekend there was a moment at 0-0 when Wirtz hit an effort wide despite having Barcola and Milos Kerkez in space on his left. It was a poor decision from a man desperate for a big moment.
Back in August, Wirtz spoke candidly about how he felt "more ready" for his second season at Anfield. The physicality was a key aspect, with bulking up a big focus of his first campaign.

"I definitely learned a lot. I just learned how Premier League football is played and I think I am more ready for my second season because I know how it is now. I am really excited for my next season," Wirtz said then.
He impressed in pre-season but two months into the new campaign, Wirtz needs to start delivering sooner rather than later.
If not, then Iraola will be left with a tough decision to make.

articles.headline: Cheap Chinese and open source LLMs could trigger trillion-dollar AI infrastructure 'reset'
keyFacts: Financial firm Jefferies reported that low-cost Chinese and open source AI models threaten to undercut US leaders like OpenAI and Anthropic.
Jefferies questioned whether major cloud providers will recoup trillions in capital spending as falling token prices impact future revenue.
Bain & Company stated the AI industry must generate six trillion dollars annually by 2031 to fund required infrastructure.
body: A financial analyst is questioning whether the collapse in AI costs owing to the arrival of Chinese, low-cost and open source models will cause a “reset” in the AI story as cloud providers struggle to recoup trillions of dollars of capital spending. In a recent research note focused on Asian markets, Jefferies estimates that about half of the roughly $2.3 trillion contracted backlog at Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Oracle is owned by OpenAI and Anthropic. Yet Chinese AI models, open source/weight and small language models, threaten to undercut the prices the two US leaders charge, casting doubt on their future revenue. Jefferies points to research from global aggregator platform OpenRouter, which found Chinese models processed 76.12 trillion tokens in the week ended 27 September, up from just 4.37 trillion in late April. The top four US providers processed 14.2 trillion tokens. Meanwhile, the launch of Moonshot AI’s open source Kimi K3 is “competing at the frontier” with an estimated 95 percent of the performance of Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5. “The question now is whether all of the above has been priced fully into markets. This writer does not think so,” the Jefferies paper states. The largest hyperscalers are set to collectively spend between $600 and $800 billion this year on building datacenters, funding it increasingly with debt rather than cash. Jefferies, however, questions where the hyperscalers' future revenue streams will come from. “It can no longer be assumed, most particularly with the arrival of the likes of Kimi K3, that large language models will ever be profitable given the related ongoing collapse in token pricing. This is extremely relevant for the hyperscalers since they have invested in datacenter capacity on the assumption that the compute will be purchased by the likes of Anthropic and OpenAI,” the paper says. While the long term bet on AI may be sound, in the medium term, there is a lot of uncertainty, it argues. “The AI story will be due for a big reset at some point in the not-so-distant future. Are the four hyperscalers really going to spend $993 billion on capex in 2027?” Jefferies questions. There are also important questions to ask about how much of the hyperscalers’ reported profits are down to their investments in AI model builders on which they will also depend for revenue. “Other income and expenses” — which describes gains in investments — have spiked in importance. Jefferies says these investments are “likely to include positions in unlisted AI-related stocks.” While the four major hyperscalers’ annualized earnings increased by $222 billion to reach $581 billion in the four quarters to 2Q26, “other non-operating income/loss” accounted for all of that increase, according to the analyst. Jefferies says “other non-operating income/loss” increased by $224 billion year-on-year to $237 billion over the same period, meaning it accounted "for all of the increase in earnings." Other research has underlined how much revenue and borrowing cloud providers might need to fund their datacenter building plans. The 2026 annual Global Technology Report from management consultants Bain & Company says the AI industry must generate $6 trillion in annual revenue by 2031 to keep funding the infrastructure needed to meet anticipated demand. That means the industry will need new uses beyond employee productivity. Bain suspects existing AI applications might make up $1.8 trillion in revenue, but this still leaves a $4.2 trillion shortfall. It could be plugged by emerging AI applications such as search engines and ads, AI-built autonomous vehicles, and AI simulations. Even if they work out, these new categories will only add up to $1.5 trillion in revenue, leaving a $2.7 trillion gap which might be filled by “new products and uses that don’t exist today.” The Register does not offer investment advice.®

articles.headline: Trump targets Ilhan Omar at rally following raid on her home – US politics live
keyFacts: US authorities conducted a predawn raid on Representative Ilhan Omar's home on Monday during an ongoing investigation, the Justice Department said.
A person familiar with the probe said it involves alleged immigration fraud, while Omar called the search political intimidation by President Trump.
President Donald Trump criticized Omar at an Ohio rally, calling her birth country of Somalia one of the worst on the planet.
body: Minnesota congresswoman Ilhan Omar said she will “not be silenced” and called a search of her Washington home part of President Donald Trump’s “intimidation” campaign.
Democratic representative Omar, an outspoken critic of the president, said she was being targeted as one of the Republican’s “political enemies”.
It comes as Trump targeted the congresswoman during a rally in Youngstown, Ohio, last night. He said Somalia, where Omar was born, is “one of the worst countries anywhere on the planet”.
He said:
She comes from one of the worst countries anywhere on the planet. What a mess they have done - Somalia.

He urged supporters to vote Republican “if you want to stop Ohio from being plundered, ransacked and destroyed like Minnesota’s being destroyed”. In response, the crowd of Republican supporters chanted: “Deport, deport.”
US authorities conducted a predawn raid of Omar’s home in Washington, DC, on Monday as part of an ongoing investigation, the Justice Department said.

A person familiar with the investigation said it is related to alleged immigration fraud, and part of the probe concerns the Somali-born lawmaker’s immigration paperwork filled out by her late father when she was a child.
Omar wrote on social media that the US government is being weaponized to target a political enemy of the president.
“For ten years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns,” she said. “This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation. I will not be silenced.”

In a statement, US House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries and other members of the party’s leadership in the chamber said the raid was “deeply disturbing and raises serious questions” about the weaponization of the federal government against Trump’s enemies.
In other developments:

A federal judge has ordered Donald Trump’s administration to temporarily halt the broadcast of taxpayer-funded television ads promoting the president ahead of the 3 November midterm elections. Effective as of 6.45pm ET on Sunday, US district judge Jennifer L Rochon of the southern district of New York issued a temporary restraining order aimed at the ads that is meant to stay in effect for at least 14 days.

The New York mayor, Zohran Mamdani, compared US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE)’s recent shooting of a man in the Manhattan enclave of Marble Hill to a mass shooting scene – and called for an end to the agency’s operations in his city. Mamdani’s joined MS NOW’s Jacob Soboroff for his first media interview since ICE agents shot and wounded Oscar Belgal, 28, during an enforcement operation while he was in his car with his five-year-old child also inside.

The Republican US senator Roger Marshall says he has finally paid off a bakery debt – after six years and repeated collection attempts reported by a Kansas business that had supplied a large order of treats for a 2020 election watch party. “We have absolutely no idea how this happened”, the Kansas senator wrote in a social media post containing a screenshot of the payment on a $678.75 invoice from Holly’s Sweet Treats as well as his $1,300 payment. “And we have repaid the bill … double.”

A businessman wanted for years in the US for allegedly paying bribes to top Venezuelan officials in exchange for lucrative state contracts in Venezuela has been taken into custody. Alvaro Pulido was indicted in Miami federal court in 2019 and again in 2021 as part of an investigation into his longtime business partner, Alex Saab, a one-time ally of ousted Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro.

There is a manic quality to Donald Trump’s desperate dash to do something, anything, ahead of November’s midterm elections to convince beleaguered Americans that he can make the pressures his policies have imposed on their livelihoods go away.

The US president offered to lower barriers against beef imports to limit surging meat prices, only to consider backtracking under pressure from the cow lobby. He offered to stop diesel exports, only to find oil companies werenot interested. He weakened fuel efficiency standards, claiming this would trim the price of a new car (and forgetting to point out it will also raise spending on gas.) In early October he started mailing $500 checks to nearly a million people touting his healthcare “wins”. Oh, and he promised adult Americans a $5,000 check if Republicans maintain control of Congress. That, too, will go nowhere.

In the face of such setbacks, maybe Trump felt he had to demonstrate he still can get something done. Still, it is somewhat counterintuitive that the administration, in the shape of Vice-President JD Vance, decided to broadcast the one initiative it did manage to bring to fruition: ejecting more than 750,000 enrollees from the Affordable Care Act (ACA) health insurance marketplaces, on grounds that they are not entitled to federal subsidies.

Trump could argue that the cuts fit within the administration’s promised commitment to restore fiscal discipline. But that part of the platform – which came as Scott Bessent, the treasury secretary, promised to trim the budget deficit to 3% of US gross domestic product – was never more than a rhetorical feint.
Most Americans think Donald Trump is profiting off the presidency in unethical or illegal ways and is focused more on his wealth than helping people like them, a new AP-NORC poll finds.

As Trump’s family business pulls in record money from new ventures helped by his policies, the survey from the Associated Press-NORC Center for Public Affairs Research finds that when it comes to allegations that Trump is profiting from the presidency, about six in 10 US adults believe he is either illegally profiting or doing something unethical but not illegal.
Only about two in 10 think the Republican president is doing nothing wrong, while a similar share say they don’t know enough to say.

At the same time, just over half of Americans say Trump has prioritized his personal financial interests “a lot” since returning to the White House, while only about one-quarter say he puts the same emphasis on the country as a whole. Few US adults, about one in 10, say he’s focused “a lot” on people like them.

The president on Friday announced that he had picked Zacharia to be the next White House press secretary, lining up a conservative commentator he called a “devoted fan” to be his most prominent spokesperson.
“It is my Great Honor to have just appointed, as Press Secretary, Katie Zacharia,” the president wrote in a social media post on Truth Social.
“She has an unblemished record of support, and has been a loyal and brilliant supporter, right from the beginning. She is, likewise, a devoted fan and member of MAGA!” Trump added.
